title: feat(auth): add under-16 family guidance flow
body:
Closes #3532

## Summary
This PR adds the client-side under-16 family guidance flow.

It is intentionally scoped to mobile UX only:
- a new welcome-screen entry point
- a deep-linkable `/account-review` flow
- an under-13 parent-or-guardian email path
- a 13-15 parental consent path that tells families to record the video outside the app and email it to `support@divine.video`

This PR does **not** add moderation backend wiring, private in-app video submission, or any DM-based consent-video flow.

## What Changed
- adds a new welcome CTA: `Not 16 yet? That's OK. Here's what you can do.`
- adds a public `account-review` route family that works from welcome or a moderation deep link later
- adds a shared explainer screen about regional rules and Divine's family-guidance approach
- adds an under-13 screen that directs parents or guardians to email `support@divine.video`
- adds a 13-15 screen that explains the parental consent video requirements and makes the path explicitly email-only
- adds deep-link parsing for `https://divine.video/account-review?source=...`
- adds focused router, deep-link, and widget tests for the new flow

## Product Boundaries In This PR
- Under 13: parent or guardian must email support. No in-app workaround.
- Age 13 to 15: the parental consent video must be recorded outside the app and emailed to support.
- Under no circumstances should a parental consent video be posted on Divine.
- DM can be wired later for moderation/support communication, but this PR does not claim that DM is a safe path for sending the video itself.

## Not Included
- moderation case creation or server state
- restricted-account enforcement from backend signals
- private media upload or encrypted video attachment support
- moderator tooling in other repos

## Main Files
- `mobile/lib/screens/auth/welcome_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_under13_support_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_parent_consent_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/router/app_router.dart`
- `mobile/lib/services/deep_link_service.dart`
- `mobile/lib/main.dart`
- `mobile/lib/l10n/app_en.arb`

## Verification
From `mobile/`:
- `flutter test --no-pub test/screens/minor_account_review_screen_test.dart test/screens/welcome_screen_test.dart test/router/login_flow_redirect_test.dart test/router/route_normalization_test.dart test/services/deep_link_service_test.dart test/router/universal_link_resolver_test.dart`
- `flutter analyze lib/screens/minor_account_review_parent_consent_screen.dart lib/screens/minor_account_review_screen.dart lib/screens/minor_account_review_under13_support_screen.dart lib/screens/auth/welcome_screen.dart lib/router/app_router.dart lib/services/deep_link_service.dart test/screens/minor_account_review_screen_test.dart test/screens/welcome_screen_test.dart`

## Follow-Up
The next phase, in other repos, is a real private submission system if we still want one:
- backend upload contract
- private storage and moderator review tools
- a separate capture/upload path with no draft save and no publish flow

title: fix(dm): split optimistic into pendingOptimistic slice (#4193)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #4193 — sent DMs were invisible in the live conversation until app restart on a freshly-searched user.
- Root cause: `_onMessageSent`'s in-memory optimistic and `_onStarted`'s watch-stream-driven projection both wrote to `state.messages`. A watch tick landing between the optimistic emit and the persistence transaction commit (the empty first tick on a fresh conversation, or any tick on a slow Keycast RPC signer) clobbered the bubble.
- Fix: move the in-flight optimistic into a new `state.pendingOptimistic` map keyed by `pendingId`. The watch path keeps replacing `state.messages` verbatim; `_onMessageSent` never touches that slice. A new `state.displayedMessages` getter merges the two for the UI.

## How the race fires (pre-fix)

1. User opens conversation → `BlocProvider` creates `ConversationBloc` with `..add(ConversationStarted())`.
2. `_onStarted` emits `(loading, [])`, then `await markConversationAsRead`, then `emit.forEach(watchMessages, …)` subscribes — `restartable()` bucket.
3. User taps send fast (typical when someone just searched a contact to message).
4. `_onMessageSent` runs in the `sequential()` bucket — concurrent with `_onStarted` — and emits `state.copyWith(messages: [optimistic, ...state.messages])`.
5. drift's `query.watch()` fires its initial tick: `[]` (no rows yet for a fresh conversation).
6. `emit.forEach.onData` replaces `state.messages` with `[]`. **Optimistic gone.**
7. `sendMessage` finishes → transaction commits → drift fires → `[persisted]` emitted. But on slow signers (Keycast RPC) or slow networks the gap between (5) and (7) is seconds. The user "observes" during that gap and sees an empty conversation.
8. Restart → fresh bloc → watch's first tick is `[persisted]` → user sees the message.

## Fix

```
state.messages           ← persisted truth, replaced verbatim by every watchMessages tick
state.pendingOptimistic  ← in-flight optimistic, keyed by pendingId, owned only by _onMessageSent
state.displayedMessages  ← getter; merges the two, preferring persisted on id collision
```

Strip rules:
- **sent / sentPartial**: remove the matching pending key. The watch tick brings the persisted row microseconds later (drift fires on transaction commit).
- **failed**: remove the matching pending key. `state.messages` stays untouched (no DB write happened).

Same `_onMessageSent` exception, retry, partial-delivery, and group-send shapes — only the slice that holds the optimistic moves. The brainstorm doc included in this PR maps the design 1:1 to #3909's planned `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)` projection, so this slice is easy to retire when that lands.

## Files

- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_state.dart` — new `pendingOptimistic` field, `displayedMessages` getter, `copyWith` parameter.
- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_bloc.dart` — `_onMessageSent` writes / strips `pendingOptimistic`; `_onStarted` unchanged.
- `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view.dart` — `_ConversationContent` selector reads `state.displayedMessages`.
- `mobile/test/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_bloc_test.dart` — state-shape + projection tests, **new race-pinning regression test driving a `StreamController<List<DmMessage>>`**, and migrated assertions on the existing send / fail / partial / group / retry / pendingId-uniqueness tests.
- `mobile/test/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view_test.dart` — new test: `MessageBubble` renders when only `pendingOptimistic` is populated.
- `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4193-dm-optimistic-watch-race-brainstorm.md` — design alternatives and rationale.

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `dart format` — clean.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/dm test/screens/inbox` — **324 / 324 passing**.

Tightened existing tests + added new ones:
- `conversation_bloc_test.dart`:
  - **NEW** `'optimistic survives a watchMessages tick that arrives mid-send (regression for #4193)'` — drives a real `StreamController<List<DmMessage>>`, pushes an empty tick during the awaited `sendMessage`, asserts `displayedMessages.length == 1` while `sendStatus == sending`. Pre-fix this would have observed `displayedMessages.isEmpty` at that frame.
  - **NEW** `'pendingOptimistic defaults to empty and participates in equality'` and `'displayedMessages projection'` group (4 tests covering empty fast-path, ordering, collision-with-persisted, unmodifiable view).
  - Migrated every send-side `s.messages.length` assertion to `s.displayedMessages.length` (user-visible) plus `s.pendingOptimistic` (in-flight tracking) so the two slices are pinned independently.
  - Rewrote the pendingId-uniqueness test to assert the strip semantics directly (`Map.remove(pendingId)`) using a seeded sibling pending — a cleaner contract than the prior list-walk-based scenario.
- `conversation_view_test.dart`:
  - **NEW** `'renders MessageBubble when only pendingOptimistic is populated (regression for #4193)'` — pumps a state with empty `messages` + non-empty `pendingOptimistic`, asserts `MessageBubble` is mounted and `EmptyConversation` is not.

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Search a fresh user via the inbox FAB on Android. Type a message. Tap send. Confirm the optimistic bubble appears immediately and stays visible.
- [ ] Verify the persisted row remains after pop + re-enter.
- [ ] Toggle airplane mode mid-send to force a failure → SnackBar shows, optimistic disappears, Retry works (existing #3908 path, no regression).

## What's deferred

- The principled fix from #3909 — `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)` at the repository layer with status-aware bubble UI — is the long-term destination. This PR is bug-scoped, and the slice it introduces maps 1:1 to the `pending` projection that #3909 will produce; switching is mechanical when the merged stream lands.

## Investigation + brainstorm

The full investigation (5-Whys, layer trace, alternative approaches, regression risk) was captured via `/investigate` and `/brainstorm` immediately before this PR. The brainstorm doc lives at `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4193-dm-optimistic-watch-race-brainstorm.md`.

title: perf(rebuilds): swap context.watch for context.select on three hot widgets
body:
## Description

`context.watch<X>()` triggers a rebuild whenever any field of `X.state`
changes, even when the widget only reads one or two of them. This PR
replaces three such call sites with `context.select` projections so each
widget rebuilds only when the data it actually consumes changes.

### `profile_videos_grid.dart`

The highest-impact site — `BackgroundPublishState` emits on every upload
progress tick, and the previous `context.watch` made the entire profile
videos grid rebuild every tick (de-duplication loop, layout, etc.) even
though it only cares about the *shape* of the active upload list.

- Project state to `List<({String draftId, String? title, String? thumbnailPath})>`
  via `context.select`. Progress is intentionally excluded so progress
  ticks no longer rebuild the grid.
- ` _VideoGridUploadingTile` now subscribes to its own upload's progress
  via `context.select<BackgroundPublishBloc, double>(...)`, so only the
  affected tile rebuilds when its progress advances.

### `video_editor_draw_item_indicator.dart`

One-line swap — only reads `selectedTool` from a 7-field state. Now
rebuilds only when the selected tool changes (was also rebuilding on
undo/redo, color, and stroke-width changes).

### `profile_header_widget.dart`

Project `MyProfileBloc` state to `(profile, isInitialOrLoading)`. The
header now ignores `isFresh` / `extractedUsername` / `verifiedClaims` /
error-variant transitions that don't affect what it renders.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3605

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` clean
- [x] `flutter test` for the three changed files (67 tests pass)
- [ ] Manual: open own profile while a background upload is in flight,
  verify the spinner advances smoothly and the grid no longer flickers
  on every progress tick.
- [ ] Manual: open the video draw editor, switch tools — indicator
  slides as before.
- [ ] Manual: open profile, observe identity skeleton → loaded

title: feat(video-player): implement the native video-player in the feed
body:
## Description This PR is an extended version of #2731 and starts implementing the native `DivineVideoPlayer` package in the home/explore feed. ~~For now, it is marked as an experimental feature and is only visible when the "New video player" option is enabled under experimental features.~~ The following will be improved with that video-player: - No preloading limitation (currently 25, adjustable). For reference: Instagram ~50, TikTok ~10 (depends on scroll speed) - Rewritten structure → removes duplication, ~80% old code can be deleted after complete migration - All video formats supported on Android (incl. HLS) - No more thumbnail fallback when swiping → smoother playback - Smaller bundle size, no ffmpeg needed - Hot restart no longer crashes - New scroll physics closer to TikTok/Instagram feel (less noticeable in debug) ### Video cache & download pipeline - **True cancel semantics for prefetch downloads.** Replaced `flutter_cache_manager`'s download path with a custom `CancellableDownloader` so cancelling a prefetch immediately tears down the underlying HTTP socket instead of letting it run to completion in the background. Frees bandwidth for higher-priority downloads when the user scrolls fast. - **Platform-native HTTP stacks for the media cache.** Switched the video/image cache from `dart:io HttpClient` (HTTP/1.1 only, isolate-local connection pool) to: - **iOS:** `cupertino_http` → NSURLSession (HTTP/2 + HTTP/3/QUIC, shared OS-level connection pool, warm TLS sessions, 0-RTT resumption, shares the pool with `AVPlayer`) - **Android:** `cronet_http` → Chromium net stack (HTTP/2 + HTTP/3, native connection pool) - **Desktop / fallback:** `dart:io HttpClient` retained for self-signed cert support in debug - Wrapped in try/catch so devices without Play Services / embedded Cronet still get a working `dart:io` fallback. - Materially faster downloads on lossy mobile connections; on iOS the player picks up warm connections opened by the cache. - **Cache files now survive app restart.** Cancellable download path persists via `store.putFile(CacheObject(...))` so cached videos remain reachable on next launch. - **Alias map for fallback URLs.** When a video is cached under a fallback key, the manifest also registers it under the stable `aliasKey`, persisted across launches — prefetcher no longer retries the failing first-attempt URL after a cold start. ## Example Video-Format HLS on Android

title: feat(dm): auto-sweep self-wrap-failed outgoing_dms via foreground retry service
body:
## Description

Closes #4124. Adds an `OutgoingDmRetryService` that sweeps the durable
`outgoing_dms` queue on every app-foreground transition and re-publishes
the missing self-wrap for any row in `recipient: sent / self: failed`
state via the `recoverSelfWrap` primitive landed in PR #4106.

Today that primitive is only invoked when the user manually taps the
partial-delivery SnackBar's Retry action. The SnackBar is ephemeral, so
dismissed taps and app-killed sessions leave self-wrap-failed rows
durably broken — silently breaking sender cross-device sync, the
*entire purpose* of NIP-17 self-wrapping.

The service mirrors `PendingActionService` one-for-one — same precedent
epic #3912 explicitly cites. It ships with a broad-shaped strategy
table but only the self-wrap-only entry wired today; rows in
`recipient: failed` state are enumerated and counted in logs to inform
the `recoverFullSend` follow-up (#4240).

**Related Issue:** Closes #4124. Follow-up: #4240. Parent epic: #3912.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Changes

**`OutgoingDmRetryService` (`mobile/lib/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service.dart`)**
- New service. Subscribes to `appForegroundProvider`. On each foreground
  transition to `true`, runs one sweep over `getRetryableForOwner`.
- Per-row backoff via `OutgoingDmRetryConfig` — defaults match
  `PendingActionRetryConfig` verbatim (5 retries, 2s → 5min, 2× backoff).
  Backoff state is durable across app kill (the DAO already writes
  `last_attempt_at` on every `markXxxWrapStatus` / `incrementRetry`).
- Re-entrancy guard: a sweep already in progress short-circuits the
  next trigger.
- Strategy dispatch:
  - **State A** (`recipient: sent / self: failed`) → `recoverSelfWrap`.
    `incrementRetry` is called only on a real publish failure so
    transient repo-not-ready states don't burn the retry budget.
  - **State B** (`recipient: failed`) → log-and-count only. Pinned via
    `verifyNever(recoverSelfWrap(rumorId: 'b'))` in the contract test.
- Error handling: `StateError` (repo not initialized) aborts the pass
  without bumping retry; `ArgumentError` (row missing / foreign owner)
  is terminal-skip; other throws bump retry and continue.

**`outgoingDmRetryServiceProvider` (`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`)**
- New `@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)` factory. Returns null when
  `userPubkey` is null OR when `isNostrReadyProvider` is false (Pattern A
  from `state_management.md` — gates dependents on readiness instead of
  catching `StateError` inside the service).
- Bridges the synchronous `appForegroundProvider` notifier into a
  `Stream<bool>` via `ref.listen(..., fireImmediately: true)` plus a
  `StreamController`, so the service contract stays free of Riverpod
  types and is easy to drive from unit tests.

**`main.dart`**
- Single `ref.watch(outgoingDmRetryServiceProvider)` at app shell setup.
  The service has no UI consumer (it operates on the durable queue), so
  without an explicit read it would never be created.

**No DAO / repository / UI / BLoC / l10n / schema changes.** The DAO is
already retry-service-ready (`getRetryableForOwner({maxRetries})`,
`incrementRetry`, durable `last_attempt_at`, per-wrap error columns —
all from PR #3911).

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `dart format` — no changes.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `mobile/test/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart` — 21
      new tests, all passing. Covers initialize/dispose, dispatch by row
      state, per-row backoff (skip / proceed / fresh), error handling
      (`StateError` aborts pass, `ArgumentError` skips row, generic
      throw bumps retry), re-entrancy guard, account scope, and
      `OutgoingDmRetryConfig.backoffFor` math.
- [x] `mobile/test/services/pending_action_service_test.dart` — 42
      tests, no regression in the precedent service.
- [x] `mobile/test/blocs/dm/` — 146 tests, no regression in DM blocs.
- [x] `mobile/packages/dm_repository` — 219 tests, no regression in
      `recoverSelfWrap`'s contract.
- [x] `mobile/test/providers/dm_repository_provider_test.dart` — 3
      tests, no regression in the DM provider's gift-wrap subscription
      lifecycle.

Pinning contracts added:
- The sweep never invokes `sendMessage` / `sendGroupMessage` / any
  recipient-publishing path (`verifyNever` on each in the
  "never republishes recipient wraps" group).
- `recipient: failed` rows are visible to `getRetryableForOwner` but
  are NOT dispatched to `recoverSelfWrap`.
- `incrementRetry` is called once per real publish failure and never
  on `StateError`/`ArgumentError` (the abort/skip paths).
- A second `sweep()` call while one is already in progress
  short-circuits without re-entering the loop.

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Force a self-wrap publish failure on a 1:1 send (e.g. block the
      second `publishEvent` round in a debug build), then **dismiss**
      the SnackBar without tapping Retry. Background and re-foreground
      the app — the row should be recovered automatically and the
      `outgoing_dms` row should be gone.
- [ ] App-kill the app between the recipient publish and the self-wrap
      publish (debug build). Re-launch. The cold-start foreground
      transition should fire one sweep; if the recipient publish had
      landed, the row should be recovered. (Caveat: a row in
      `recipient: pending / self: pending` state — i.e., we don't yet
      know whether the recipient publish landed — is out of scope for
      this PR's filter; it's covered by #4240's follow-up.)
- [ ] On a long foreground session, observe the per-row backoff in
      logs: `skipped-backoff=N` should grow as the same row gets
      re-evaluated within its backoff window.

## Brainstorm + plan

The design rationale (why a foreground-only trigger; why the broad
service shape with only self-wrap-only recovery wired today; why
mirror `PendingActionService` instead of putting the loop inside
`DmRepository`) is captured in
`mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4124-outgoing-dm-auto-sweep-brainstorm.md`,
included in this PR.

title: DM: auto-sweep recipient-sent / self-wrap-failed rows in outgoing_dms
body:
## Summary

`outgoing_dms` queue rows can persist in `recipient: sent / self: failed` state when the user dismisses the partial-delivery SnackBar without tapping Retry, kills the app before retry, or both bookkeeping writes fail in `recoverSelfWrap` after a successful publish. Today these rows only progress when the user manually re-taps Retry — there is no automatic sweep.

## Problem

The user-facing UX assumes Retry is the only recovery surface, but the queue row is the durable source of truth and outlives the SnackBar. Without a sweep:

- A self-wrap publish that fails silently (relay outage, transient network) stays unfixed across app launches.
- Sender cross-device sync — the entire purpose of the self-wrap — is silently broken until the user reopens that conversation, sees no SnackBar, and never knows to retry.

## Desired Outcome

Periodically sweep `outgoing_dms` for rows where `recipient_wrap_status == sent && self_wrap_status == failed` and call `DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap(rumorId)` for each.

## Scope

- Decide cadence: app foreground, conversation enter, or a periodic timer. App-foreground is the cheapest signal that maps to "user is around if a relay round-trip is needed."
- Bound the work: rate-limit attempts per row (e.g., min N seconds between retries), cap total attempts before backing off (the row already records `lastError`).
- Verify the sweep cooperates with `recoverSelfWrap`'s idempotent `selfWrapStatus == sent` guard so a manual Retry mid-sweep doesn't republish.

## Context

- Recovery primitive landed in #4106 (closes #4102); what's missing is automatic invocation.
- Called out during PR #4106 review as a follow-up gate before merge.

title: rfc(cache_sync): design and prototype a unified low-level stale-while-revalidate cache package
body:
> **Related:** #2313 – the feed-side consumer work depends on this package existing first.

## Decision

In #2313 the team reached consensus ([@rabble](https://github.com/rabble), [@NotThatKindOfDrLiz](https://github.com/NotThatKindOfDrLiz)): we want a **unified low-level cache** at the repository/data layer so that **the UI and BLoC layers never need to know about caching details**. This issue is the RFC and prototype track for that package.

---

## What `cache_sync` is

A thin internal Flutter package that wraps any network `Future` or `Stream` and turns it into a **stale-while-revalidate stream**: the local DB is emitted first (instant), then silently replaced once the network responds.

The pattern is identical regardless of what data is fetched – REST feed results, follower lists, profile metadata. Repositories call one method; the package handles everything else.

---

## Core API shape

```dart
enum CacheFetchPolicy { cacheAndNetwork, cacheOnly, networkOnly }

class CacheResult<T> {
  const CacheResult.cached(this.data) : isLive = false;
  const CacheResult.live(this.data)   : isLive = true;
  final T    data;
  final bool isLive; // false = showing cache; true = network responded
}

abstract class CacheSync {
  // Future-based (REST / single-shot) – emits cached result first, then live
  static Stream<CacheResult<List<T>>> watch<T>({
    required String cacheKey,
    required Future<List<T>> Function() fetch,
    required List<T> Function(String json) fromJson,
    required String Function(List<T> data) toJson,
    CacheFetchPolicy policy = CacheFetchPolicy.cacheAndNetwork,
    Duration? ttl,
  });

  // Single-entity variant
  static Stream<CacheResult<T?>> watchOne<T>({
    required String cacheKey,
    required Future<T?> Function() fetch,
    required T? Function(String json) fromJson,
    required String Function(T data) toJson,
    CacheFetchPolicy policy = CacheFetchPolicy.cacheAndNetwork,
    Duration? ttl,
  });

  // Stream-based (WebSocket / Nostr relay – items arrive one-by-one)
  static Stream<CacheResult<List<T>>> watchStream<T>({
    required String cacheKey,
    required Stream<T> Function() subscribe,
    required List<T> Function(String json) fromJson,
    required String Function(List<T> data) toJson,
    CacheFetchPolicy policy = CacheFetchPolicy.cacheAndNetwork,
    Duration? ttl,
  });

  // Explicit invalidation (e.g. after a write operation or logout)
  static Future<void> invalidate(String cacheKey);

  // Scoped invalidation – deletes all keys with a given prefix
  static Future<void> invalidatePrefix(String prefix);
}
```

---

## Storage model: blob-per-key

**Decision: blob-per-key (JSON) in a dedicated `CacheEntries` Drift table.**

Rationale:
- The existing `db_client` typed tables (`NostrEvents`, `UserProfiles`, etc.) own their own schemas and are not touched by `cache_sync`.
- `cache_sync` targets opaque REST responses (like `HomeFeedCache`) that don't map to an existing typed table.
- A single generic table keeps `cache_sync` self-contained with no cross-package schema coupling.

```dart
// Drift table inside mobile/packages/cache_sync/lib/src/
class CacheEntries extends Table {
  TextColumn get cacheKey  => text()();               // primary key
  TextColumn get payload   => text()();               // JSON blob
  DateTimeColumn get cachedAt => dateTime()();        // write timestamp
  DateTimeColumn get expiresAt => dateTime().nullable()(); // null = no TTL

  @override
  Set<Column> get primaryKey => {cacheKey};
}
```

`CacheDao` exposes three methods only:
```dart
abstract class CacheDao {
  Future<CacheEntryRow?> getCached(String key);
  Future<void> upsert(String key, {required String payload, DateTime? expiresAt});
  Future<void> delete(String key);
  Future<void> deleteByPrefix(String prefix); // for logout / account switch
}
```

Consumers never import Drift. The `CacheSync` static methods are the only public surface.

---

## Answered RFC questions

**1. Fit with existing local storage**
`cache_sync` sits *alongside* the existing `db_client` typed tables. It does not replace `NostrEvents`, `UserProfiles`, or any other typed table. It fills a specific gap: opaque REST response caching where no typed Drift row already exists.

**2. Key scoping and invalidation**
Cache keys must be prefixed with the active account's pubkey hex:
```dart
// In the repository, not in cache_sync itself:
final key = '${pubkeyHex}:home_feed:global';
```
On logout or account switch, call `CacheSync.invalidatePrefix(pubkeyHex)` to wipe all entries for that account. `cache_sync` provides `invalidatePrefix`; the repository is responsible for calling it at the right time.

**3. Storage model** — answered above (blob-per-key).

**4. Refresh failure UX**
If the network call throws, `watch`/`watchOne`/`watchStream` emit nothing after the cached result — the stream simply doesn't emit a live `CacheResult`. The BLoC stays on cached state and treats the error via its normal `addError` path. `CacheResult` does **not** get an `error` field; error propagation is the repository's job.

**5. TTL / staleness**
Explicit `invalidate`/`invalidatePrefix` is the primary mechanism. TTL (`Duration? ttl`) is optional and passed per call-site. At read time, if `expiresAt` is in the past, the entry is treated as a miss and deleted. No background sweep needed for now.

**6. Worked example**
See implementation plan below — the pilot migration of `HomeFeedCache` serves as the worked example.

---

## Package skeleton

```
mobile/packages/cache_sync/
├── lib/
│   ├── cache_sync.dart                  # top-level barrel
│   └── src/
│       ├── cache_dao.dart               # abstract DAO interface
│       ├── cache_dao_impl.dart          # Drift-backed implementation
│       ├── cache_entries_table.dart     # Drift table definition
│       ├── cache_fetch_policy.dart      # enum
│       ├── cache_result.dart            # CacheResult<T>
│       ├── cache_sync.dart              # CacheSync static methods
│       └── cache_database.dart          # DriftDatabase with CacheEntries
├── test/
│   ├── cache_dao_test.dart
│   ├── cache_result_test.dart
│   ├── cache_sync_watch_test.dart
│   ├── cache_sync_watch_one_test.dart
│   ├── cache_sync_watch_stream_test.dart
│   └── cache_sync_invalidate_test.dart
└── pubspec.yaml
```

`pubspec.yaml` dependencies: `drift`, `path`, `path_provider`.  
No dependency on `db_client`, `models`, or any feature package. Self-contained.

---

## Implementation order

1. **`pubspec.yaml`** – create package, add to workspace `pubspec.yaml`
2. **`cache_entries_table.dart` + `cache_database.dart`** – Drift table and in-memory test DB helper
3. **`cache_dao.dart` + `cache_dao_impl.dart`** – DAO interface and Drift implementation + tests (`cache_dao_test.dart`)
4. **`cache_result.dart` + `cache_fetch_policy.dart`** – plain Dart, no Drift + tests
5. **`cache_sync.dart`** – `watch`, `watchOne`, `watchStream`, `invalidate`, `invalidatePrefix` + tests for each
6. **`cache_sync.dart` barrel** – export public surface only
7. **Pilot migration**: replace `HomeFeedCache` (SharedPreferences) in `video_feed_bloc.dart` / `videos_repository` with `CacheSync.watch` + key `'${pubkeyHex}:home_feed:global'`
8. **Delete `HomeFeedCache`** and `serveCachedHomeFeed`/`_cacheServed` in the same PR (tracked in #2313)

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six RFC questions above are answered ✅ (done in this issue)
- [ ] Package lives under `mobile/packages/cache_sync/`
- [ ] Public API (`CacheSync`, `CacheResult`, `CacheFetchPolicy`) is finalized and documented
- [ ] Drift-backed storage is encapsulated – consumers import only `cache_sync`, never `drift` or `cache_sync/src/`
- [ ] `watch`, `watchOne`, `watchStream` are implemented and tested
- [ ] `invalidate` and `invalidatePrefix` are implemented and tested
- [ ] TTL eviction on read is implemented and tested
- [ ] Pilot migration: `HomeFeedCache` replaced with `CacheSync.watch` (unblocks #2313)
- [ ] 100% line coverage on the package (strict-coverage gate, see `testing.md`)
- [ ] `HomeFeedCache` deletion and BLoC cleanup land in the **same PR** as the pilot migration

title: task(feed): decide and implement repository-owned persistent cold-start feed cache
body:
## Problem

On `main`, cold-start feed caching is still handled by a special-case `HomeFeedCache` in the BLoC layer for the home feed. That gives us some cached startup behavior, but it is not the right architectural shape and it is not a clean repository-owned source of truth.

Relevant current code on `main`:
- `mobile/lib/blocs/video_feed/home_feed_cache.dart`
- `mobile/lib/blocs/video_feed/video_feed_bloc.dart` (`serveCachedHomeFeed`, `_cacheServed`)

This leaves us with two open problems:
1. **Cold-start UX**: feed startup still depends on ad hoc caching behavior instead of a consistent repository/data-layer strategy.
2. **Tech debt**: feed caching lives in the BLoC layer instead of the repository layer, and the old `HomeFeedCache` path remains a one-off exception.

## Why This Matters

- Users should be able to reopen the app and see feed content immediately, without always waiting for the first network response.
- Feed caching should be owned by the repository/data layer, not by BLoC-only special casing.
- The current shape makes cache consistency and future feed-mode expansion harder than it should be.

## Current State In `main`

- `HomeFeedCache` is still present and BLoC-owned.
- The cold-start cache path is still special-cased rather than repository-owned.
- In-memory feed caching exists, but persistent cold-start caching is not cleanly consolidated in the repository layer.

## Decision Needed

Do we still want persistent feed caching as a product behavior?

If yes, the expected direction is:
- repository-owned persistent cache
- DB-backed rather than BLoC-local special casing
- clean cold-start behavior with clear cache invalidation / refresh semantics
- removal of the old `HomeFeedCache` path once replaced

If no, we should explicitly close this issue and accept the current network-first / special-case-cache behavior rather than leaving the debt half-acknowledged.

@rabble @hm21 tagging you both for direction on whether we still want to pursue this and, if so, what the preferred product / architecture shape should be.

## Decision (reached 10–11 May 2026)

**Yes** – unified low-level cache, repository-owned, UI/BLoC layer stays unaware of caching details.

RFC and prototype work tracked in **#4244**.

This issue remains scoped to the **feed consumer side only**: replace `HomeFeedCache` with the unified repository-owned cache and delete `HomeFeedCache` in the same PR. This work is blocked on #4244.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide whether persistent cold-start feed caching is still desired ✅
- [ ] Move persistent feed-cache ownership into the repository/data layer (depends on #4244)
- [ ] Remove the old BLoC-layer `HomeFeedCache` special case in the same PR
- [ ] Define which feed modes should participate in persistent cold-start caching
- [ ] Define refresh / invalidation behavior clearly enough to implement without new cache debt
- [ ] Land with tests that cover cold-start read, cache write, and refresh behavior

## Prior Attempt

PR #2417 was an earlier draft attempt at this work. It is no longer the right merge vehicle and should be treated as historical context only, not as the branch to revive.

title: fix(video-editor): improve audio gaps between clips
body:
## Description

Users reported on Discord that loops in diVine didn’t feel as smooth as they did on Vine. This PR updates the `pro_video_editor` to improve looping from the rendering side by using a single audio track across the entire video instead of multiple tracks. This fixes the gaps between clips and at the end of the video, but it does NOT solve the gap when the loop restarts.

The current MediaKit solution CANNOT handle seamless looping, so a small gap will always remain. Once we merge the new native video players in #3242, this issue will also be fixed since they use the correct native playback implementation for this use case.

The only possible workaround with MediaKit would be running two video players at the same time, but since the app already reaches its limits with a single MediaKit player, that is not a viable option.

title: fix(profile): adjust memCacheWidth calculation for profile-tab thumbnails
body:
Closes #4221



## Description

PR #4191 was merged with an unresolved review comment about thumbnail decoding performance — the very issue that PR was meant to optimize.

## Problem

#4191 introduced a hardcoded `memCacheWidth = 400` for profile tab thumbnails. In practice, the actual rendered tile width (in physical pixels) varies between **~160 and ~600 px** depending on device size and `devicePixelRatio`:

- On small / low-DPR devices: we decode **more pixels than the tile can show** → wasted RAM and CPU on every grid item.
- On large / high-DPR devices: we decode **fewer pixels than the tile shows** → upscaled, blurry thumbnails.

A single static value cannot satisfy both ends of the device spectrum.

## Fix

Compute `memCacheWidth` from the actual tile constraints at build time:

```dart
LayoutBuilder(
  builder: (context, constraints) {
    final dpr = MediaQuery.devicePixelRatioOf(context);
    final memCacheWidth = (constraints.maxWidth * dpr).round();
    return VineCachedImage(memCacheWidth: memCacheWidth, ...);
  },
)
```

This guarantees each device decodes thumbnails at exactly its required resolution — no waste, no upscaling.

## Notes

- `memCacheHeight` is intentionally left unset; setting both axes triggers `ResizeImagePolicy.fit` to pick the tighter axis, which causes portrait thumbnails to upscale under `BoxFit.cover`.
- A follow-up may bucket the computed width (e.g. nearest 32 px) to avoid re-decodes on window resize on web/desktop.

title: DM: add recoverFullSend primitive for recipient-wrap-failed outgoing_dms rows
body:
## Summary

`outgoing_dms` rows can land in `recipient_wrap_status: failed / self_wrap_status: failed` state when the recipient gift-wrap publish itself fails (set by `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart`). Today there is no recovery primitive for this state — only `recoverSelfWrap` exists (PR #4106), and it is for the `recipient: sent / self: failed` case only.

## Problem

The new `OutgoingDmRetryService` from #4124 enumerates these recipient-failed rows and logs a count, but does not act on them. They sit on the queue until the user manually re-sends, or until `retry_count` reaches `maxRetries` and they fall out of the retryable filter. The `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` comment ("both wrap statuses remain retryable on the queue row") promises auto-retry that does not yet exist.

## Desired Outcome

Add a `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` primitive that re-runs the full `sendRumor` (recipient + self) for a stored row, persisting `direct_messages` on success and updating queue-row status by outcome — the same shape as `sendMessage`'s success and partial paths.

Wire the primitive into the `OutgoingDmRetryService` strategy table as the second entry: `recipient: failed` rows dispatch to `recoverFullSend`.

## Scope

- New `NIP17MessageService.publishFullSend` (or reuse `sendRumor` directly) for an already-built rumor — same integration shape as `publishSelfWrap` from PR #4106.
- New `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` that:
  - Looks up the row by id, validates ownership (mirror `recoverSelfWrap`'s account-scope check).
  - Rebuilds the rumor from `rumor_event_json`.
  - Calls `sendRumor` (or `publishFullSend`).
  - On success: runs the same `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` + atomic `direct_messages` insert that `sendMessage` does on its happy path.
  - On failure: marks both wraps `failed` and bumps retry — same shape as `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure`.
  - Idempotent: short-circuits if `recipientWrapStatus == sent` (a prior recovery already landed and the row has since been demoted to a self-wrap-only retry case — call `recoverSelfWrap` instead).
- Strategy-table wiring in `OutgoingDmRetryService` so `recipient: failed` rows are recovered the same way `recipient: sent / self: failed` rows are today.
- Tests pin: no double-publish to recipient if the prior attempt's recipient publish actually landed but local persistence failed; no duplicate `direct_messages` row inserted; sweep dispatches the right primitive per row state.

## Edge cases to design carefully

- **Recipient publish actually landed but local persistence failed last time.** The previous `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` marks both wraps failed pessimistically — in this case, `recoverFullSend` would re-publish to the recipient. The receiver-side NIP-17 dedup keys on rumor id (preserved across retries via `rumor_event_json`) bound this to a duplicate gift wrap rather than a duplicate visible message, but it is still wasted bandwidth. Decide whether the design should query the relay for the rumor-id-tagged gift wrap before re-publishing.
- **App killed mid-publish (`pending: pending` rows).** Out of scope for #4124's `getRetryableForOwner` filter; covered by `getStillPendingForOwner` instead. Decide whether `recoverFullSend` covers both cases (state B and state C from the brainstorm) or whether state C gets its own primitive.

## Context

- Brainstorm that surfaced this gap: `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4124-outgoing-dm-auto-sweep-brainstorm.md`.
- Production telemetry will come from #4124's enumeration log (`Log.info('OutgoingDmRetryService sweep complete: ... recipient-failed=N')`). Use those counts to prioritize this work.
- Sister issue #4127 covers Crashlytics surfacing for the doubly-degraded paths inside `recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` — coordinate so this work does not duplicate that error-reporting decision.
- Parent epic: #3912 (DM reliability hardening).

title: task: fix mobile_service_integration_tests workflow so e2e tests actually run
body:
## Context

Discovered during review of #4234 (cc @hm21).
`.github/workflows/mobile_service_integration_tests.yaml` exists and runs `--tags service`, but is structurally broken on three independent axes — even with a correctly-tagged `patrolTest`, no test will execute.

## Problems

1. **Wrong runner**: the step runs `flutter test integration_test/e2e/ --tags service`. Patrol tests need `patrol test` (which orchestrates the native automator + device bootstrap). `flutter test` against a `patrolTest` body either silently no-ops or errors out depending on the patrol version.
2. **No device**: `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` with no Android emulator (e.g. `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner`) and no iOS simulator. Patrol's native automation requires a booted device for the `Selector(...)` taps and `platformAutomator` actions.
3. **Trigger**: `on: workflow_dispatch` only — never fires from `push` / `pull_request`, so even a fixed workflow would not gate PRs without a manual run.

Combined effect: the `--tags service` filter is moot today because the workflow can't successfully run any patrol test. The four existing tests in `mobile/integration_test/e2e/` (`c2pa_init_test.dart`, `deleted_video_visible_to_other_users_test.dart`, `dm_optimistic_survives_watch_race_test.dart`, `video_creation_flow_test.dart`) are also missing the `service` tag — file a tag-pass once the workflow runs.

## Proposed fix (for whoever picks this up)

- Switch the `Run service integration tests` step to `patrol test --target integration_test/e2e/ --tags service` (or whatever flag set matches the project's patrol version).
- Add `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2` (or equivalent macOS-runner + iOS simulator setup) to provision a device before the test step.
- Add `pull_request` and/or `push` triggers, scoped to paths that affect e2e behaviour.
- Tag the four existing tests in `mobile/integration_test/e2e/` with `tags: ['service']` once the workflow actually executes them — this lets the `--tags service` filter behave as documented.

## Acceptance

- A PR that touches code under e2e coverage triggers the workflow.
- The workflow boots a device, runs `patrol test`, and the four (now five, post-#4234) tests in `integration_test/e2e/` all execute.
- Failing the new test in #4234 from a regression of the watch-stream race actually fails the workflow.

## Out of scope

- Repairing this workflow is **not** in scope for #4234. That PR's only obligation is to add the `service` tag for forward-compat, which it does.

title: fix(notifications): restore PR #3548 row styling and l10n on top of video grouping
body:
Closes #4184 ## Description PR [#3548](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3548) ("new-notifications", merged 2026-04-29) shipped a Figma-aligned notifications redesign: a 32×32 type-icon column with an accent palette, inline `labelLargeFont` emphasis on actor names and titles, an `outlineDisabled` row border, and a localized date section header. PR [#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944) (video grouping + thumbnails, 2026-05-05) reimplemented the row from scratch and dropped all of those styles. Subsequent fixes ([#3828](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3828), [#4007](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4007), [#4013](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4013)) further regressed the view container background, the date section header, and several l10n call sites. A separate small drift slipped the inbox conversation-tile preview color from `onSurfaceVariant` to `onSurfaceMuted`. This PR re-applies the PR #3548 visual language on top of the current sealed-type / grouping / thumbnail functionality. It does not change any behavior introduced by [#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944), [#3961](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3961), [#3828](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3828), [#4007](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4007), [#4013](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4013), or [#4130](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4130) (replies routing). The actor row's inline `Text.rich` layout includes a `_verbFor` branch for `NotificationKind.reply` so the verb produced by [#4130](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4130) renders correctly under the new row structure (bold actor span + `notificationRepliedToYourComment` plain span + inline timestamp). ### Notifications screen
Main This branch
**Related Issue:** Relates to [#3548](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3548) ## Type of Change - [ ] ✨ New feature - [x] 🛠️ Bug fix - [ ] ❌ Breaking change - [x] 🧹 Code refactor - [ ] ✅ Build configuration change - [ ] 📝 Documentation - [ ] 🗑️ Chore ## What changed - `ActorNotificationRow` and `VideoNotificationRow` now use `NotificationTypeIcon` with the original `accentPink` / `accentLime` / `accentViolet` / `accentYellow` palette (`likeComment` and `reply` fall into the heart and chat accents respectively). - Row container restored: uniform `surfaceContainerHigh` background + `outlineDisabled` bottom border. Unread state shows the red dot on the type icon, not a row-level tint. - `ActorNotificationRow` uses `UserAvatar` (the placeholder-avatar primitive from PR #3548) instead of a hand-rolled `CachedNetworkImage` stack. The Follow back button uses `DivineButton(size: tiny)` and the `notificationFollowBack` l10n key instead of a hand-rolled `FilledButton` with hardcoded `'Follow back'`. - `_MessageText` restored on both rows: `labelLargeFont` emphasis on actor names and video titles, `bodyMediumFont` verbs, `onSurfaceMuted55` trailing relative timestamp via `LocalizedTimeFormatter.formatRelative`. The actor row's `_verbFor` includes a `reply` branch returning `notificationRepliedToYourComment` directly (no actor-placeholder strip needed) so the bold actor + reply verb render correctly under the new structure. - Date section header restored: `VineTheme.labelLargeFont(color: onSurfaceMuted)` + `LocalizedTimeFormatter.formatDateLabel`. - Restored l10n on five snackbar / failure body strings that #3944 / #4007 hardcoded (`notificationsVideoNotFound`, `notificationsVideoUnavailable`, `notificationsFromNotification`, `notificationsFailedToLoad`, `notificationsRetry`). - Dropped the inline `Divider` between rows; the row's bottom border owns the separation again. - New `notification_type_icon_spec.dart` helper as the single source of truth for the `NotificationKind` → `(icon, accent pair)` mapping. Locked by a regression test so a future reskin can't silently drift the row palette. - `ConversationTile` last-message preview color restored to `onSurfaceVariant`, with a regression test pinning the color so the same drift can't recur silently. `VideoNotificationRow` keeps the 56×56 thumbnail introduced by #3944 — kept as new functionality, not a regression. ## New widget extractions (not restoration) The diff is sized as a "restoration" but three files in `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/` are net-new code worth reviewing as such, not as restored content: - **`notification_comment_quote.dart`** (+59 LOC) — shared primitive for the `"…" 2d` quote-with-trailing-timestamp pattern. Owns the timestamp suffix when a comment quote is present so the trailing relative time stays anchored to the visual end of the row regardless of whether a quote is rendered. - **`notification_leading_type_icon.dart`** (+43 LOC) — shared wrapper combining `notificationTypeIconSpec` with `NotificationTypeIcon`. Replaces an 11-line private widget that was duplicated byte-for-byte across both row variants. - **`notification_video_thumbnail.dart`** (+74 LOC) — public extraction of the previously-private `_Thumbnail` inside `VideoNotificationRow`. Content was relocated, not invented; the file is new but the widget itself existed in the merge base. Surfaced so tests can use `find.byType` instead of a magic-string `Key` (per `testing.md` "Prefer Type Over Key"). Each of the three has a focused widget test in `mobile/test/notifications/widgets/`. ## Non-goals (preserved unchanged) - Sealed split `VideoNotification` / `ActorNotification` and grouping logic ([#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944)). - The `kindFilter` parameter (Likes tab still matches both `like` and `likeComment`). - d-tag / addressable-id navigation ([#4007](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4007)) and the realtime enrichment path ([#3944](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3944)). - Reply / likeComment tap routing and the model accepting `reply` ([#4130](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4130) — landed on main during the lifetime of this PR; the actor row's reply verb is the only piece restored here so the inline `Text.rich` layout renders the right text). - Inbox-open badge sync via Riverpod cache ([#4165](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4165)). - The collab-invite plaintext suppression in `_MessageList` and the `_previewText` replacement in `ConversationTile` ([#3672](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3672)). - The legacy `mobile/lib/screens/notifications_screen.dart` and `mobile/lib/widgets/notification_list_item.dart` (test-only, dead code in production) — out of scope; deleting them is a separate follow-up. ## Test plan - [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test packages` — clean - [x] `dart format` — clean - [x] `flutter test test/notifications/ test/widgets/notification_type_icon_test.dart test/widgets/notification_list_item_test.dart test/screens/inbox/inbox_view_test.dart test/screens/inbox/inbox_page_test.dart test/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart test/screens/notifications_navigation_test.dart test/screens/notifications_refresh_test.dart packages/divine_ui/test/src/button/divine_button_test.dart` — green - [x] `divine_ui` strict-coverage gate maintained: `divine_button.dart` 121/121 line coverage with the new `DivineButtonSize.tiny` variant - [ ] Manual: notifications tab matches Figma — accent palette + dot + border (in **dark mode** — Divine is dark-mode only) - [ ] Manual: a comment-like (`likeComment`) row uses the heart accent - [ ] Manual: a reply row uses the purple chat-bubble accent + "{actor} replied to your comment" - [ ] Manual: grouped video like row shows thumbnail and stacked avatar - [ ] Manual: Follow back button on a follow row uses `DivineButton(size: tiny)` and is flush with the avatar (no row-height jump on tap) - [ ] Manual: long-press on system row does nothing (kept behavior) - [ ] Manual: Spanish locale shows localized snackbar copy - [ ] Manual: inbox conversation list shows preview text in `onSurfaceVariant`

title: feat(divine_ui): extract IdentitySkeletonizer + pilot on comment item
body:
Closes #4230

## Description

Follow-up to #4183. Extracts the identity-loading skeleton state machine
that PR #4183 tightened in `_ProfileHeaderWidgetState` — `Timer` +
`_wasLoadingIdentity` guard + post-frame schedule + 7 s fallthrough — into
a new reusable widget under `divine_ui`, and pilots it on the comment
author row.

**`mobile/packages/divine_ui/lib/src/skeleton/identity_skeletonizer.dart` (new)** —
`IdentitySkeletonizer({required bool isLoading, required Widget child,
Duration fallthroughTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 7)})`. Same
behaviour as the inline state machine on the profile header: shimmer
while `isLoading`, dissolve after `fallthroughTimeout` so users with no
Kind 0 see the underlying generated-name fallback instead of an infinite
shimmer. Caller derives `isLoading` from its own loading source.

**`mobile/lib/screens/comments/widgets/comment_item.dart`** — pilot site.
Comment events carry only the pubkey (no `authorName` field), so until the
Kind 0 arrives every comment renders
`UserProfile.generatedNameFor(authorPubkey)` — the same
misleading-placeholder failure mode #4163 fixed for the profile screen.
Wraps the avatar + name row in
`IdentitySkeletonizer(isLoading: profile == null, ...)`. Pointer events on
the author-tap gesture are absorbed during the loading window — consistent
with the profile-header avatar's tap behaviour shipped in #4183.

**Tests** — strict-coverage gate satisfied at 100 % line coverage on the
new `divine_ui` file (7 widget tests covering: enabled-flip on isLoading
transitions, timeout dissolve via `tester.pump(Duration)`, pending-timer
cancel on isLoading=false, rapid-rebuild idempotence, dispose-during-
pending-timer, default 7 s timeout). Comment-item test pins the
`IdentitySkeletonizer.isLoading=true` invariant while the profile is null.

**Out of scope** — `_ProfileHeaderWidgetState` migration to the new
widget, DM conversation header, notifications. Each is its own follow-up

title: ci(codemagic): clean stale Xcode/SPM workspace state before iOS builds
body:
Closes #4236

## Summary

The Codemagic iOS archive step intermittently dies with:

> `** INTERNAL ERROR: Unable to load workspace 'Runner.xcworkspace' **`
> `Uncaught Exception: *** -[NSMutableArray insertObjects:atIndexes:]: count of array (53) differs from count of index set (52)`
> `IDESwiftPackageCore … sortedInsert(of:) … registerDependencyFileReferences …`

Root cause is a desynced `Runner.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/workspace-state.json` carried over within a single Codemagic build — the iOS workflow opens the workspace three times (`flutter build ios --config-only`, `pod install`, `flutter build ipa`), and Xcode 16's `IDESwiftPackageCore` occasionally trips on a stale SPM graph from the earlier opens.

## Fix

Add a shared `clean_ios_workspace_state` step that wipes:
- `$HOME/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`
- `ios/Pods` and `ios/.symlinks`
- `ios/Runner.xcworkspace/xcuserdata`
- `ios/Runner.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm`

…before each iOS workflow runs, so the archive step always sees a freshly-resolved SPM graph. Wired into `ios-build`, `ios-simulator-build`, and `e2e-smoke-ios`. `Podfile.lock` is intentionally left in place so pod resolution stays reproducible across CI runs.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run the `iOS Build` workflow on Codemagic from this branch and confirm the archive completes
- [ ] Re-run a few times — the failure was intermittent, so a single green run isn't proof
- [ ] `iOS Simulator Build` workflow still passes
- [ ] `E2E Smoke Tests (iOS)` workflow still passes

title: feat(video): show likers/reposters list when owner taps like/repost
body:
Closes #4173

## Summary
- Tapping Like or Repost on your own video used to toggle your own like/repost — meaningless on a video you authored. It now opens a full-screen list of the users who liked or reposted that video instead.
- Adds a new repository method on each engagement-tracking package (`likes_repository.fetchEventLikers`, `reposts_repository.fetchEventReposters`) that pulls reactor / reposter pubkeys directly from relays. Funnelcake's REST API only exposes aggregate engagement counts, so the lists have to come from a kind 7 / kind 6+16 relay query, deduped across `e` / `a` tags and with kind 5 deletions filtered out.
- New `VideoEngagementBloc` + `VideoEngagementListScreen` (Page/View) at `/video/:eventId/likers` and `/video/:eventId/reposters`, with an optional `?a=` query param for addressable Kind 30000+ events. The list reuses the existing `UserProfileTile` (without the follow CTA) for rendering.
- Threads `isOwnVideo` from the existing check in `VideoOverlayActionColumn` down into `LikeActionButton` and `RepostActionButton`. On the owner's own video, the tap navigates instead of dispatching the toggle event.

## Known limitations / follow-ups
- The lists are loaded once when the screen opens (single relay query, returns when EOSE fires). They don't subscribe for live updates of new likes / reposts that arrive while the screen is open. Pull-to-refresh re-runs the query. Eventually we'll want a live-subscription-backed list and pagination once it matters; this v1 ships the full list because most own-video engagement counts are small.
- Five new ARB keys (`videoEngagementLikersTitle` / `RepostersTitle` / `LikersEmpty` / `RepostersEmpty` / `LoadFailed`) are added in English and allowlisted in `arb_consistency_test.dart` so non-English locales fall back to English until the next translation pass — same pattern as the recent Edit / Report button additions.

## Test plan
- [ ] As the video author, tap the Like button on your own video → likers list opens; back returns to the feed; refresh re-queries.
- [ ] As the video author, tap the Repost button on your own video → reposters list opens; tapping a profile pushes their profile screen.
- [ ] As another user, tap Like on someone else's video → still toggles like (count flips, heart fills).
- [ ] As another user, tap Repost on someone else's video → still toggles repost.
- [ ] Empty-state copy renders when no one has liked / reposted yet.
- [ ] Failure state renders + retry works when the relay query fails.
- [ ] Both addressable (Kind 34236 with d-tag) and non-addressable target events work — the addressable id is forwarded as `?a=` and merged with the `e`-tag results.

title: feat(profile): upload a banner image from the profile setup screen
body:
Closes #4233

## Summary

- Adds a 3:1 banner image preview + upload UI on the profile setup screen, alongside a banner-scoped color picker.
- Uses the new bloc-driven upload pattern (mirrors the avatar's `pendingPictureUrl` / `persistedPictureUrl` shape).
- Image and color are mutually exclusive; selecting one clears the other at the bloc layer.
- Pre-fills from any existing `profile.banner` set in another Nostr client (URL or hex color).
- New ARB strings translated to all 17 locales (en + 16 non-English).

## Why

`profile_setup_screen` already lets users edit a banner *color* and the rest of the app already *renders* banner images set in other Nostr clients — but divine-mobile users couldn't *upload* an image themselves and had to leave the app to update a banner.

## Architecture

- `ProfileEditorBloc` gains `InitialPersistedBannerSet`, `ProfileBannerUploadRequested`, `ProfileBannerColorSelected`, and `ProfileBannerCleared` events; `PendingBannerStatus` + `BannerUploadError` enums; `pendingBannerUrl` / `pendingBannerColor` / `persistedBanner` state fields; and an `effectiveBanner` getter.
- `_saveProfile` reads `state.effectiveBanner` (staged URL > staged color > persisted) so the UI no longer threads `banner:` through `ProfileSaved`.
- Save is gated on `pendingBannerStatus != uploading` (parallel to the avatar gate) so kind 0 isn't published with a stale banner.

## Test plan

- [ ] Camera + gallery on Android — same.
- [ ] Toggle from color → image → color and confirm previews + Save payload.

- [ ] Pre-existing hex banner pre-selects the matching color swatch.

title: fix(profile): show skeleton for username/avatar during profile load
body:
## Description

Fix #4163 by replacing the centered "Loading profile…" text card with a layout-shaped skeleton, and scoping the in-screen profile-header skeleton to just the avatar + name/NIP-05/bio block.

**`profile_loading_view.dart` (rewrite)** — drops the `Center → Column(text + spinner)` placeholder and renders a single top-level `Skeletonizer` over a layout that mirrors the real post-load shape (banner area, avatar, identity block, stats row, action row, tab bar, video grid). No more visual pop when the real screen mounts.

**`profile_header_widget.dart`** — wraps just the avatar and the name/NIP-05/bio block in a single `Skeletonizer` driven by `isLoadingIdentity`. Stats row and action buttons sit outside the skeleton so they stay tappable during the loading window. A 7-second timeout dissolves the skeleton even when the parent still says "loading," so users with no Kind 0 fall through to the existing generated-name / identicon path instead of shimmering forever. Cached-profile short-circuits (`MyProfileLoading(profile: cached)`, supplied `widget.profile`) avoid warm-start shimmer. Timer mutation is deferred to a post-frame callback so `build()` stays pure.

**ARB cleanup (in scope, tightly coupled)** — `profileLoadingTitle` / `profileLoadingSubtitle` are dead the moment `ProfileLoadingView` renders no text. Splitting them into a separate PR would leave `main` with two l10n keys that have zero callsites. Dropped from all 18 locale files and the generated localization sources.

**Tests** — `profile_header_widget_test.dart` adds the `Identity skeleton (#4163)` group covering all five own-profile state transitions, the supplied-profile short-circuit, the 7-second dissolve, and the "stats row + action buttons stay outside the skeleton" invariant. `profile_loading_view_test.dart` is updated to assert the new skeleton shape.

title: fix(inbox): show DM unread badge on Messages segment toggle
body:
## Summary

Closes #4216.

The bottom-nav inbox dot is a sum of unread notifications + unread DMs (`vine_bottom_nav.dart:97-99`), but the inbox UI only surfaced the notifications count via the segmented toggle's `notificationCount` field. Users with unread DMs saw the dot persist after clearing notifications and read it as "the dot didn't reset" — there was nowhere in the UI to learn that DMs were the cause.

Mirror the existing notification-side plumbing on the Messages side: add `messageCount` to `InboxSegmentedToggle` and wire it from `DmUnreadCountCubit.state` in `InboxView`.

## What changes

- `InboxSegmentedToggle` gains a `messageCount` parameter (defaults to `0`, same shape as `notificationCount`). Both sides now surface their count via the existing `_NotificationBadge`.
- `InboxView` watches `DmUnreadCountCubit.state` and forwards it to `messageCount`.

## Out of scope

Already in place — verified during investigation:
- Per-conversation unread dot (`_UnreadDot` in `conversation_tile.dart:172-186`). Once a user opens Messages they can see which conversations are unread; this PR provides the segment-level signal that gets them there.

## Tests

Two new tests in `inbox_view_test.dart`:
- `forwards DmUnreadCountCubit state to InboxSegmentedToggle.messageCount`
- `forwards relayNotificationUnreadCountProvider to InboxSegmentedToggle.notificationCount`

Both pin the wiring so a future regression where `messageCount` falls back to `0` (the cause of the original bug) fails loudly.

All 14 inbox view tests pass; full `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` clean.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/screens/inbox/inbox_view_test.dart`

title: Inbox bottom-nav dot stays lit after clearing notifications when DMs are unread (no DM count surfaced anywhere)
body:
## Summary

Users report "my notifications didn't reset after I tapped the inbox." The actual cause: the bottom-nav inbox dot is a **sum** of unread notifications + unread DMs, but the inbox UI only surfaces the notification count. There is no count anywhere telling the user that DMs are still unread.

So when a user taps the Notifications tab and clears it, the bottom-nav dot stays lit because of unread DMs. From the user's POV they "cleared" something but the dot persists with no explanation.

## Trace

The dot is computed in `mobile/lib/widgets/vine_bottom_nav.dart:97-99`:

```dart
int _inboxUnreadCount(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
  final dmCount = context.watch<DmUnreadCountCubit>().state;
  final notifCount = ref.watch(relayNotificationUnreadCountProvider);
  return dmCount + notifCount;
}
```

The segmented toggle inside the inbox (`mobile/lib/screens/inbox/widgets/inbox_segmented_toggle.dart`) only takes `notificationCount` — there is **no `messageCount` field on the toggle**. The Messages side has no badge, ever.

`InboxView` does watch `relayNotificationUnreadCountProvider` for the notifications-side badge but never reads `DmUnreadCountCubit` for a messages-side badge.

(Per-conversation unread dots `_UnreadDot` already exist in `conversation_tile.dart:172-186`, so once a user does open the Messages tab they can see which conversations are unread. The missing piece is the segment-level summary that tells them to look there at all.)

## User experience walkthrough

1. User has 3 unread notifications + 5 unread DMs. Bottom-nav dot is lit.
2. User taps Inbox. Sees segmented toggle: `Notifications [3]` and `Messages` (no badge).
3. User taps Notifications. The `[3]` clears.
4. Bottom-nav dot is **still lit** because the 5 unread DMs were never touched.
5. From the user's perspective: "I cleared notifications. Why is the dot still there?" They have no signal that the Messages side is the cause.

## Fix

Add a `messageCount` field to `InboxSegmentedToggle` (mirror of the existing `notificationCount` plumbing) and wire it from `DmUnreadCountCubit.state` in `InboxView`. PR coming.

Out of scope (already in place):
- Per-conversation unread dot in `conversation_tile.dart` ✅

title: fix(router): safe pop fallback so empty-stack back buttons land on home feed

labels.name: needs-issue
labels.description: PR needs a linked tracking issue

body:
## Scope

This PR is **introduce-the-helper + migrate the dominant crash site**, plus a bundled CI fix. There are ~28 other `context.pop()` callers in `mobile/lib/screens` that are latent for the same crash class. They are not migrated here so this stays reviewable; follow-ups can sweep them once this lands.

## Summary

Fixes the dominant Crashlytics issue [`5c465b01...`](https://console.firebase.google.com/u/0/project/openvine-co/crashlytics/app/ios:co.openvine.app/issues/5c465b01bb5421f294ecca1adaaf440a?time=7d) — `Fatal Exception: FlutterError - GoError: There is nothing to pop` (928 events / 161 users in the last 7 days; 78% in profile flows; iOS 26).

**Root cause.** `KeyManagementScreen` is a top-level `GoRoute` (`/key-management`). When a caller navigates with `go` / `goNamed` / a deep link, the matched hierarchy collapses to `[/key-management]` and the AppBar's bare `onBackPressed: context.pop` throws on the next tap. PR #3941 (May 5) added a high-traffic entry point — `profile_setup_screen.dart`'s "view public key" link used `context.goNamed(KeyManagementScreen.routeName)`, which reset the back stack — explaining the recent 1.0.11 / 1.0.12 spike. The Apr 14 (1.0.8) regression is the older underlying weakness for any other empty-stack path (deep link, double-tap, etc.).

## Changes

Three concerns; calling them out separately for review:

**1. New helper (defense-in-depth, applies to all top-level routes)**
- `lib/extensions/safe_pop_extension.dart` — `context.safePop({String? fallback})`. Checks `canPop()` first; falls back to `defaultSafePopFallback` (`/home/0`) or a caller-supplied route instead of crashing.
- `key_management_screen.dart` — AppBar back button and post-import dismiss now use `context.safePop`.

**2. Proximate fix in profile-setup (separate behaviour change)**
- `profile_setup_screen.dart` L2222 — "view public key" link flips from `goNamed` to `pushNamed`. This is a deliberate behaviour change: `pushNamed` adds to the stack so the back arrow returns to the profile editor (preserving unsaved edits) instead of resetting. This is what PR #3941 intended; `goNamed` was the bug.
- `profile_setup_screen.dart` L417-429 — replaces an existing `try/catch (e) { context.pop() }` block with a `canPop()` guard. Same fallback semantics (go to `/profile/$npub` when authenticated, else `/home/0`); just stops using exception flow for control flow.

**3. Bundled CI fix — repo-wide preview-deploy break (helps the *next* PR after this merges, not this one)**
- `.github/workflows/mobile_pr_preview_deploy.yml` — pass `--commit-hash`/`--commit-message=$HEAD_SHA` explicitly to wrangler. Without these flags, `cloudflare/wrangler-action`'s `pages deploy` falls back to `git log -1` of the workflow's checkout — which on `workflow_run` is *main's* tip, not the PR head. Cloudflare's API has been rejecting main's current message — `Invalid commit message, it must be a valid UTF-8 string [code 8000111]` — apparently because wrangler 3.90.0 mojibakes the em-dashes in commit `0585d82e` (#4106) on Ubuntu runners. Every PR triggered after #4106 merged has been failing the deploy step (build is green; only the deploy and the comment that follows are broken). ASCII-only SHAs sidestep it.
  - **Important caveat:** GitHub runs `workflow_run` workflows from the **default branch's** copy of the YAML, so this change does *not* affect this PR's own deploy. Once this PR merges to main, all subsequent PRs will pick up the fix. Bundling here rather than separately because the change is one line and the rationale is the same investigation.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze` clean on the four touched files
- [x] New extension tests pass (6/6)
- [x] Existing `key_management_screen_test.dart` and `profile_setup_screen_test.dart` still pass (45/45)
- [ ] Manual: open app via deep link to `/key-management`, tap back → lands on home feed (no crash)
- [ ] Manual: edit profile → "view public key" → back → returns to edit profile (preserved stack)
- [ ] Post-merge verification: next PR triggered after merge should produce a fresh "Mobile PR Preview" comment instead of failing on `Invalid commit message`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Sweep remaining ~28 `onBackPressed: context.pop` call sites (auth/nostr_connect, library, video_detail, other_profile, etc.) onto `context.safePop`.
- Consider making `DiVineAppBar`'s default back behaviour `safePop` so future top-level screens are protected by construction.
- Audit `mobile_web_production_deploy.yml` for the same `--commit-message` gap.

title: feat(l10n): complete translation across all 17 non-English locales
body:
## Description

Closes the entire `_knownUntranslatedDebt` allow-list in
`mobile/test/l10n/arb_consistency_test.dart` (149 keys at start of
this PR) and removes the constant entirely. The consistency test
now enforces "every locale defines every template key" with no
exceptions.

The work spans three logical phases that landed across 7 commits on
this branch:

1. **PR 1 cleanup** (`e7a2c1a0d`): dropped 153 keys that were
   already translated in every mature locale but kept on the
   allow-list defensively. After this commit Filipino — added
   partial via [#4097](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4097) —
   was the only locale missing those keys.

2. **PR 2 small batches** (`f04227270` … `d0d11bf3c`): translated
   the remaining 110 small-batch keys across the 16 mature locales
   where listed (mostly `de`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `nl`, `pt`) and
   added all 110 to `app_fil.arb`. Total: 156 cells.

3. **PR 3 full passes** (`c36bd1c59`): translated the 39 keys that
   were missing or English-valued in every locale. Covers Video
   Settings Menu (a11y popover), Video Action Report/Edit, Report
   Reason Subtitles + Learn More (App Store compliance), Video
   Editor – Audio Picker, Sounds Library, and Support Log Export.
   600 cells across 17 locales.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3814

## Translation method

Same pattern as [#4097 (Filipino)](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4097)
and [#2986 (Bulgarian)](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/2986):
Claude (Sonnet 4.5) per-string translation briefed on
`brand-guidelines/TONE_OF_VOICE.md` and each locale's existing
neighbouring strings.

Style invariants enforced across every locale:

- ICU placeholders (`{count}`, `{title}`, `{path}`, plurals)
  preserved verbatim
- ALL CAPS section headers preserved where the source uses them
- Brand and product nouns (Divine, Loops, Sounds, Revine, Featured)
  kept in English where each locale's existing tech-app convention
  does
- Filipino: `i-` prefix for English-rooted action verbs, informal
  pronouns (`mo`, `ka`, `iyong`)
- Apple-compliance copy (CSAM, AI-generated, copyright) uses
  legal-precise terminology rather than colloquial paraphrases

## Quality caveat — read before merging

Translation quality varies by locale. From the LLM's perspective:

- **High confidence**: en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pt
- **Medium confidence**: id, ja, ko, ar — solid grammar but
  UI-tone calibration may want a native-speaker pass
- **Lower confidence**: am, bg, pl, ro, sv, tr — meaning-correct
  but some idiom choices may read stiff

For App Store-critical strings (`reportReason*Subtitle`, especially
`reportReasonCsamSubtitle`), I used legal-conservative phrasings
rather than colloquial ones — that's the safer compliance default.
A native review pass on the lower-confidence locales is recommended
before App Store submission, but the translations are correct
enough to ship as a baseline.

A few mature-locale `sound*` keys had pre-existing non-EN
translations that differed from my proposed values; the apply
script preserved those (visible in the commit's translation
warnings). All ARB consistency tests pass; `flutter gen-l10n`
reports zero untranslated messages across all locales.

title: build(ci): add macOS lane for iOS attestation RunnerTests
body:
Closes #4119. Follow-up to #3979.

## Summary

Adds a `runner-tests` job to `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` that runs the Swift `RunnerTests` suite from #3979 on `macos-14` so regressions in `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` or `FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler.eventPayload` fail CI instead of relying on a contributor remembering to run `xcodebuild test` locally.

## Why

The Nostr bridge attestation work is a security-sensitive boundary. The two types this PR gates are:

- `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` — single-instance attach/detach state machine that prevents the per-frame attestation handler from being silently dropped or swapped.
- `FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler.eventPayload` — pinned contract that the Dart-bound payload contains exactly `{message, isMainFrame}` and never leaks origin host/port/scheme upward.

Without a CI lane these tests are honor-system. This PR makes them required.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml`:

- New `runner-tests` job on `macos-14` with Xcode `15.4` pinned via `maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1`. Flutter `3.41.9` matches the existing Ubuntu jobs verbatim.
- Steps: `flutter precache --ios` → `flutter pub get` → `flutter build ios --config-only --no-codesign` (writes `Generated.xcconfig` so the Podfile resolves `FLUTTER_ROOT`) → CocoaPods cache keyed on `Podfile.lock` → `pod install` → `xcodebuild test -only-testing:RunnerTests` against an iPhone 15 simulator.
- Code signing is disabled (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, `CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO`) — simulator unit tests don't need a profile.
- On failure the `.xcresult` bundle is uploaded as an artifact for triage.
- `mobile-ci` aggregator now `needs: runner-tests` and exits non-zero if it fails, so the lane becomes transitively required by branch protection without any branch-protection rule change.

No `paths:` filter — runs on every PR to `main`, matching the existing workflow's convention. The cost (~5–7 macOS minutes per PR) is acceptable for a security-critical lane.

## Test plan

- [ ] First run on this PR is green; `runner-tests` and `mobile-ci` both pass.
- [ ] Push a throwaway commit that flips one expected `AttachResult` case in `RunnerTests.swift`; verify `runner-tests` goes red, `mobile-ci` goes red, the other five jobs stay green; revert.
- [ ] Confirm the PR is blocked from merge while red (branch protection on `mobile-ci`).
- [ ] Inspect the failing run's `RunnerTests.xcresult` artifact and verify it opens in Xcode.

body:
Closes #4227

## Summary

Combines two orthogonal fixes that have each been deadlocked in their own PR (each blocked by the bug the *other* fixes). Shipping both in one PR so CI can go green in a single run without bypass-merging.

**Closes the deadlock between #4222 and #4224 — both will be closed in favor of this PR.**

## Changes

### 1. Revert #4128 — drop the broken iOS Runner Tests lane

The lane has been red on every PR (and on \`main\` itself) since #4128 merged. Root cause: an SPM workspace-load race in Xcode 26.x's \`IDESPMWorkspaceDelegate.dependencyPackagesDidUpdate\` that crashes \`xcodebuild\` with \`count of array (53) differs from count of index set (52)\` before any test executes.

Reproduced on both Xcode 26.3 (the original pin) and 26.2 (verified on a closed experimental PR — same crash, same stack frames). A 16.x downgrade isn't viable: \`pro_video_editor 1.15.0\`'s \`CompositionBuilder.swift\` references \`AVVideoCompositionLayerInstruction.Configuration\`, an iOS 26 SDK type that Swift type-checks at compile time.

Re-land #4128 once Apple ships an Xcode 26.x without the SPM race (watch for 26.4) or once the \`macos-26-arm64\` runner image is available with a working Xcode. This loses the \`NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy\` regression gate in the meantime.

### 2. Restore \`PathProviderPlatform.instance\` in seed-media test \`tearDown\`

#4154 ("fix(test): re-enable Bucket E skipped tests #3137", commit \`5a525e7bf\`) removed \`@Tags(['skip_very_good_optimization'])\` from \`mobile/test/services/seed_media_preload_service_test.dart\`, putting it back into the merged VGV optimized-isolate run.

That file's \`setUp\` mutates \`PathProviderPlatform.instance\` to a \`MockPathProviderPlatform\` configured only with a temp path — but its \`tearDown\` never restores the original. The leaked mock has no application-documents path set, so subsequent files in the same isolate (notably the top-level group of \`draft_storage_service_test.dart\`) call \`getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()\` against the leaked mock, and \`path_provider\` throws \`MissingPlatformDirectoryException(Unable to get application documents directory)\` — 19 \`DraftStorageService\` tests fail.

The fix mirrors the save-and-restore pattern already used by \`upload_initialization_helper_test.dart\` and the \`migrateOldDrafts\` sub-group of \`draft_storage_service_test.dart\` itself.

## Test plan

- [x] **Local repro:** ran \`flutter test test/services/seed_media_preload_service_test.dart test/services/draft_storage_service_test.dart\` together in CI order. Goes from 19 \`MissingPlatformDirectoryException\` failures → all 32 tests passing.
- [x] **CI on #4224 (just the test fix, before combine):** \`Tests\`, \`Generated Files\`, \`Format\`, \`Analyze\` all green; only \`iOS Runner Tests\` was red, and that lane is removed by part (1) of this PR.
