title: revert(ci): drop iOS Runner Tests lane (#4128) due to Xcode 26.x SPM crash
body:
Closes #4223

## Summary

Reverts #4128. The new `iOS Runner Tests` lane has been red on every PR — and on `main` itself — since it merged. This unblocks the CI queue.

## Root cause

Xcode 26.x has an SPM workspace-load race in `IDESPMWorkspaceDelegate.dependencyPackagesDidUpdate` that crashes `xcodebuild` with `count of array (53) differs from count of index set (52)` before any test executes. The same `IDEGroup insertGroupSubitems:atIndexes:context:` stack frames appear on every run.

Verified on both versions available on `macos-15-arm64`:
- **26.3** (the original pin in #4128) — crashes
- **26.2** (#4218, now closed) — same crash, identical signature

## Why not a different pin

A downgrade to Xcode 16.x isn't viable: `pro_video_editor 1.15.0`'s `CompositionBuilder.swift` references `AVVideoCompositionLayerInstruction.Configuration`, an iOS 26 SDK type. The reference is runtime-gated (`if #available(iOS 26.0, *)`), but Swift type-checks both branches at compile time, so the SDK has to ship the type.

26.1.1 / 26.0.1 are also installed on the runner but are in the same Xcode-26 family that introduced this regression, so trying them is at best speculative.

## Tradeoff

This loses the `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` regression gate that #4128 added. Re-land #4128 once either:
- Apple ships an Xcode 26.x without the SPM race (watch for 26.4), or
- GitHub ships a `macos-26-arm64` runner image with a working Xcode, or
- A workaround for the workspace-load race is found (e.g. running `xcodebuild` with a pre-resolved `.xcresolved` to skip the workspace-load path that's racing).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `mobile-ci` aggregate green (the `RunnerTests` lane no longer exists, so it can't be the blocker).
- [ ] CI: other lanes (`Tests`, `Analyze`, `Format`, `Generated Files`) unaffected.

Note: there is a separate `Tests` failure on `DraftStorageService` that is also red on `main`. That's not addressed by this revert and needs its own fix PR — investigation in progress.

body:
Closes #4219

## Summary

- Downgrades the iOS Runner Tests lane in `mobile_ci.yaml` from Xcode 26.3 → 26.2.
- Restores the `RunnerTests` lane (and the `mobile-ci` aggregate) that has been red on every PR since #4128 merged, including on `main` itself.

PR #4128 added the macOS `RunnerTests` lane and pinned it to Xcode 26.3 because `pro_video_editor 1.15.0`'s `CompositionBuilder.swift` references `AVVideoCompositionLayerInstruction.Configuration` — an iOS 26 SDK type. The crash reproduces on `origin/main` head independent of any PR diff — see [comment on #4128](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4128#issuecomment-4414556243).

26.2 ships the same iOS 26 SDK without the SPM race. `macos-15-arm64` already has 26.2 installed alongside 26.3, so the pin change is a one-line swap with no infra cost.

A 16.x downgrade isn't an option — `pro_video_editor` requires the iOS 26 SDK at compile time. Reverting #4128 wholesale would also drop the `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` regression gating that the lane provides; this surgical pin keeps the gate intact.

title: fix(perf): cap profile-tab thumbnail decode size to keep ImageCache from thrashing
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `memCacheWidth: 400` constraint to `ProfileTabThumbnail`'s `VineCachedImage`. The cap mirrors the existing pattern in `video_notification_row.dart` and is sized for 3-column phone tiles at 3.2× pixel ratio.
- Without it, `cached_network_image` decodes thumbnails at native CDN resolution (~3 MB each); a 50+ tile profile grid overflows Flutter's default `ImageCache` budget, thrashes the cache, and stalls first paint by ~1s.
- Single-file production change; benefits every profile tab grid that shares the widget (videos / liked / reposts / saved / collabs / comments).

Surfaced by @hm21 on [PR #4182 review](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4182#pullrequestreview-4257513564).

Closes #4190.

## Why this scope

The two related perf issues — #3603 (de-dup in `build()`) and #3605 (`context.watch` on `BackgroundPublishBloc`) — only affect the **own-profile-with-active-uploads** path. The reviewer's repro is opening *another user's* profile, where `isOwnProfile=false` makes both no-ops. The dominant cost in that path is image decode + `ImageCache` thrash on first paint of the 50-event relay burst, which this PR addresses directly. Both related issues remain open for their assignees.

If QA still observes residual jank after this lands, the next layer to look at is the provider-side cascade in `profile_feed_provider.dart` — `_relayVideosSnapshot()` re-sorts the bucket on every relay tick (`video_event_service.dart:886-887`) and `filterVideoList` does two O(N) passes per emit (`video_event_service.dart:633-697`). That refactor needs its own scoping and is intentionally out of scope here.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile/` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart` — 9 / 9 pass (8 existing + 1 new pinning `memCacheWidth == 400` and `memCacheHeight == null` so `BoxFit.cover` still scales proportionally).
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/` — 170 / 170 pass.
- [ ] Manual: cold-launch app, open a profile with **50+ videos**. Compare loading-spinner-clear → first-tile-painted timing before/after. Confirm no >16ms frames during the burst (Performance overlay).
- [ ] Manual: open own profile + retained-state path (re-open same profile) + a profile with <10 videos to confirm no regression in the small-grid case.

## Related (not addressed here)

- #3603 — Move profile grid de-duplication out of `build()` (open, assigned).
- #3605 — `context.watch` causing unnecessary widget rebuilds (open).

title: fix(perf): profile videos tab feels laggy for ~1s when opening profile with 50+ videos

labels.name: performance
labels.description: App startup, video playback, rendering, and memory

body:
## Summary

Opening another user's profile with 50+ videos shows a ~1s freeze right after the loading spinner clears, before the grid becomes interactive. Surfaced in [PR #4182 review](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4182#pullrequestreview-4257513564) by @hm21.

> *"does it also feel super laggy for you when opening the profile of someone who has 50+ videos when everything is loaded for maybe 1s? It's definitely not caused by this PR, so if you notice it too, it's probably something we should tackle in a separate PR."*

## Repro

1. Cold-launch the app, sign in.
2. Navigate to a profile with **50+ videos** (the `subscribeToUserVideos` limit is 50, so this is the boundary case where all events arrive in a single relay EOSE burst).
3. Observe: the loading spinner clears, then the screen freezes for ~1s before the videos grid responds to scroll/tap.

## Root cause analysis

Three contributing layers; only #1 affects the *other-user* repro the reviewer flagged:

1. **Image-decode + `ImageCache` thrash on first paint of 50 thumbnails** *(primary, affects all profile types)*
   - `mobile/lib/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail.dart:32` wraps `VineCachedImage` **without a `memCacheWidth`** constraint.
   - Without it, `cached_network_image` decodes thumbnails at native CDN resolution (typically 720×1280 ≈ 3 MB each). 50 tiles × ~3 MB ≈ 150 MB, which exceeds Flutter's default `ImageCache` budget (100 MB / 100 entries) → cache thrashing, repeated decodes, and a heavy GPU-upload spike on first paint.
   - Precedent in-repo: `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/video_notification_row.dart:164` already uses `memCacheWidth: 200` for 56dp tiles.

2. **`ProfileVideosGrid.build()` rebuild churn on `BackgroundPublishBloc` progress ticks** *(own-profile only)*
   - Already tracked in #3605 (item #1).

3. **De-dup + `DateTime.now()` parsing + side-effecting `downloadFile()` inside `build()`** *(own-profile only)*
   - Already tracked in #3603.

For the reviewer's specific repro (opening *someone else's* profile), `isOwnProfile=false` makes #2 and #3 no-ops. The 1s lag is dominated by #1, plus the relay-burst provider work in `_relayVideosSnapshot` → `authorVideos` (re-sorts the entire bucket on every call, `mobile/lib/services/video_event_service.dart:886`) → `filterVideoList` (two O(N) passes, `video_event_service.dart:633-697`).

## Proposed fix (scoped to this issue)

Add `memCacheWidth` to `ProfileTabThumbnail`'s `VineCachedImage`. Single-file change benefits **every** profile tab grid that shares the widget (videos / liked / reposts / saved / collabs / comments).

The deeper provider-cascade work (`authorVideos` re-sort, double-pass `filterVideoList`, multiple state-emit re-renders during cold-load) is out of scope for this fix and should be triaged separately if QA still observes residual jank after the decode fix.

## Related work (not duplicated here)

- #3603 — Move profile grid de-duplication out of `build()` (open, assigned).
- #3605 — `context.watch` causing unnecessary widget rebuilds (open, calls out `profile_videos_grid.dart`).

title: fix(perf): cache BlurhashDisplay decode future across rebuilds
body:
## Description

`BlurhashDisplay` constructed a fresh `_createImageFromPixels(...)` future inside its `build()` method. Each parent rebuild created a new `Future` (different identity), so `FutureBuilder` treated it as a fresh request and re-showed the gradient fallback while the new decode completed. On a 50+ tile profile grid churning under `BackgroundPublishBloc` upload-progress emissions (tracked in #3605), this multiplied into visible flicker across the whole grid plus redundant `decodeImageFromPixels` calls per visible tile.

This was surfaced on low-end Android in @hm21's [review of PR #4191](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4191#pullrequestreview-4257933582), as one of three layers of residual jank that PR's `memCacheWidth` cap didn't address.

### Fix

Cache the decode future in `State` so its identity stays stable across rebuilds, and recompute it only when `blurhash` / `contentType` actually change:

- New `Future<ui.Image?>? _imageFuture` field on `_BlurhashDisplayState`.
- `_decodeBlurhash()` now constructs the future once when new `BlurhashData` arrives, alongside `_blurhashData`, inside the existing `setState`.
- `build()` reads `_imageFuture` instead of constructing a new one each call.

Single-file production change (+12 / -6). Test added pinning the new invariant.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4196

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib/widgets/blurhash_display.dart test/widgets/blurhash_display_test.dart` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/blurhash_display_test.dart` — 1/1 pass (new test asserts `same(future)` across a parent rebuild).
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart test/widgets/video_thumbnail_widget_test.dart` — 20/20 pass (existing tests that exercise `BlurhashDisplay` via its callers).
- [ ] Manual: open a profile with **50+ videos** + an active upload (own profile). Confirm gradient fallback no longer flickers across grid tiles during upload-progress ticks. Compare against `main`.

## Related (not addressed here)

- #3605 — `context.watch<BackgroundPublishBloc>` rebuilding the whole grid on every progress tick (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz). Reducing rebuild frequency is the bigger lever; this PR makes each rebuild cheaper while waiting for that fix.
- #3603 — Move profile grid de-duplication out of `build()` (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz).
- #4191 — `memCacheWidth` cap on the network image (decode-cache thrash). Independent layer of the same lag report.

**The chips:** Right Now · Today · This Week · This Month · All Time

- **Right Now** keeps the current behavior — `/api/videos?sort=watching` (24h CDN view count, no age decay).
- **Today / This Week / This Month / All Time** route through funnelcake's `/api/leaderboard/videos?period=…` endpoint (newly wired into the funnelcake client).

**Architecture** (per `.claude/rules/architecture.md`):
- UI chip taps push URL changes (`context.go('/explore/tab/popular?period=<slug>')`)
- `ExploreScreen.didChangeDependencies` syncs `?period=` from `GoRouterState` into a Riverpod `StateProvider<LeaderboardPeriod?>` (post-frame to avoid build-phase writes)
- `popularVideosFeedProvider` watches the StateProvider; period flip triggers a fresh `_loadFirstPage`
- `VideosRepository.getPopularVideos({period: ...})` dispatches to `/api/leaderboard/videos` when period is set, falls through to existing watching/NIP-50 path when null
- A sealed `_PopularCursor` (timestamp vs offset) keeps pagination semantics straight across the two paths

**URL format:**
- `/explore/tab/popular` — Right Now (default)
- `/explore/tab/popular?period=today|week|month|alltime` — windowed leaderboard

`fromUrlSlug` accepts both `today` and `day` for back-compat; the canonical emit is always `today` for shareability.

**l10n:** 6 new keys (label + 5 chip names) added to `app_en.arb` only; allowlisted in `_knownUntranslatedDebt` in `arb_consistency_test.dart`. Translations land in a follow-up locale-pass PR.

## What's NOT in this PR

A **New / Classics** content axis on the Popular tab is intentionally **out of scope**. The combination `Classics × {Today,Week,Month,All Time}` is server-blocked: `/api/leaderboard/videos` silently ignores unknown query params (verified by live probe — `?platform=vine` returns identical bytes to the bare query) and the response items don't include a `platform` field at all, so client-side filtering also isn't possible.

The funnelcake-side ask is to:
1. Add `platform=` query support to `/api/leaderboard/videos` (matching `/api/videos`)
2. Include `platform` in the leaderboard response items

Once that ships, the kind axis can land as a small follow-up PR (one `popularKindProvider`, one chip row, no new endpoint plumbing).

`Right Now × Classics` works today via the existing `?sort=watching&platform=vine` combo and could ship in this PR — but it'd be a half-feature ("kind axis only available on Right Now") with confusing UX, so we're holding the entire kind axis until the server work lands.

## Test plan

Automated:
- Funnelcake client: 10 new tests covering URL construction, all 4 period wire values, offset pagination, response edge cases, error paths
- Repository: 5 new tests covering period dispatch, offset propagation, no-NIP-50-fallback semantics, period-keyed cache, watching-path regression
- Provider: 3 new tests covering period propagation, default null behavior, rebuild-on-flip
- Widget (`PopularFilterBar`): 6 tests covering chip rendering, selected state, URL push, urlSlug-vs-wireValue distinction, Right Now clears `?period=`
- Widget (`PopularVideosTab`): 1 smoke test that the filter bar renders above the grid
- Screen (URL → provider sync): 5 tests covering ?period=week, today-slug back-compat, bare URL clears, invalid value, no-GoRouter no-op
- l10n consistency: existing test extended with the 6 new keys
- **Full mobile suite**: 8344 pass / 400 skip / 0 fail post-rebase

Manual (still needed before merge):
- [ ] Tap each chip on a real device, verify URL updates and grid refreshes
- [ ] Deep-link `/explore/tab/popular?period=week` from cold start, verify correct chip is selected and grid loads
- [ ] Background the app for 10s, return — verify selected chip survives
- [ ] Verify scroll-to-hide animation works for the new chip row alongside the existing trending hashtags row
- [ ] Pull-to-refresh on each window — confirm correct endpoint is hit (network logs)
- [ ] Test with `flutter run` in different system text scales — chip row should grow with text, not clip

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Notes

- Implementation plan is committed at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-08-popular-tab-time-period-filter.md` for future maintainers.
- The popular feed provider keeps its private cursor field (refactored to a sealed `_PopularCursor`) — extending the existing legacy Riverpod pattern rather than introducing a BLoC migration. Future cleanup item.
- Cache key changed from `'popular'` to `'popular:<wireValue>'` for windowed periods; the Right Now path keeps the bare `'popular'` key for backward compatibility.
- 4 fix commits included: cursor/period race guard, accessibility-safe ConstrainedBox, layout-safety in unbounded parents, GoRouter-absence no-op. Each addresses an issue caught by automated review during plan execution.

title: fix(profile): preserve arbitrary Kind 0 fields across profile edits
body:
## Summary

Closes #4175.

Editing a profile silently dropped any Kind 0 field the typed `UserProfile` model didn't know about — `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, `bot`, NIP-39 `i` tags, custom client keys, future NIP additions. PR #4022 patched the symptom for `nip05` only; this PR generalizes the fix to every field.

## What changes

### Two-layer fix

1. **`ProfileRepository.saveProfileEvent` now seeds from the freshest relay Kind 0** before composing the new event content. Relay events round-trip through `UserProfile.fromNostrEvent`, which preserves the full content as `rawData` — so unknown fields survive byte-identical. Falls back to `currentProfile` on relay timeout/failure.
2. **`UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound` now mirrors the typed REST fields into `rawData`** (defense-in-depth — kicks in when the relay fetch fails). The Funnelcake REST API does not expose the raw Kind 0 JSON, so unknown fields can only be recovered via the relay seed.

### Merge contract

The new `saveProfileEvent` builds the published content from a copy of `seed.rawData`, then applies a small set of explicit deltas:

- **Editable fields** (`display_name`, `about`, `picture`, `banner`): caller's value wins. Empty/null **removes the key** — the form is pre-populated from the seed, so an empty submit is treated as an explicit clear.
- **`nip05`**: keeps the race-protected clear semantics from #4022 — only removed when `clearNip05: true`.
- **Every other key**: passes through from the seed untouched.

Also drops the previous behavior of writing explicit `null` for unset editable fields; those keys are now omitted entirely. Semantically equivalent on all major Nostr clients, and consistent with how unknown-field preservation works (no key === unset).

## Why this matters

A divine-mobile user who edits their bio in our app no longer silently rewrites their Kind 0 in a way that erases work done in any other client (Damus, Amethyst, Primal, etc.). Lightning zaps via `lud16` keep working. NIP-39 identity proofs survive. Future NIPs that we don't yet model survive automatically.

## Tests

The load-bearing invariant is pinned by a new test in `profile_repository_test.dart`:

> "preserves arbitrary unknown fields when seeded from a relay-fetched Kind 0"

The seed has `bot`, `i`, `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, and a `weird_future_field`. Editing only `display_name` produces a published event whose every non-`display_name` key is byte-identical to the seed.

Other new tests:
- `falls back to currentProfile when relay seed fetch fails`
- `mirrors typed REST fields into rawData` (`user_profile_test.dart`)
- `omits null typed fields from rawData` (`user_profile_test.dart`)

Existing `saveProfileEvent` tests were updated for the new omit-empty-keys contract. The #4022 nip05 preservation regression test was kept intact.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test` in `mobile/packages/models` — 103 passing
- [x] `flutter test` in `mobile/packages/profile_repository` — 195 passing
- [x] `flutter test mobile/test/blocs/profile_editor/` — 71 passing
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile/` — clean
- [ ] Manual: log in as a user with `lud16` set in another client; edit display_name in divine-mobile; inspect published Kind 0 via `wss://relay.divine.video` — confirm `lud16` is present.

## Out of scope

- Funnelcake REST returning the raw Kind 0 event JSON — would let the typed REST factory carry unknown fields too. Track in `divine-funnelcake`. Until then, the relay seed step is the only path that preserves unknown fields.
- Same `rawData`-loss pattern on other replaceable kinds (kind 3 follow lists, kind 10002 relay lists, kind 10000 mute lists). Worth a survey but not in this PR.

title: Profile edits silently drop lud16, lud06, website, and other Kind 0 fields when loaded from REST API
body:
## Summary

Editing a profile silently strips every field beyond the explicit form inputs (`display_name`, `about`, `nip05`, `picture`, `banner`) when the loaded `currentProfile` came from the Funnelcake REST API. Most notably this means **lightning addresses (`lud16`, `lud06`)** and **`website`** disappear from the user's published Kind 0 the next time they edit any profile field.

This is the **same root cause** that #4021 / #4022 fixed for `nip05` specifically, generalized to every other field. The earlier fix added a one-off fallback for nip05 only, so today nip05 is preserved but lud16/lud06/website/bot/etc. are not.

## Root cause

`UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound` in `mobile/packages/models/lib/src/user_profile.dart:99` populates the typed fields from the REST response but sets `rawData: const {}`:

```dart
factory UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound(UserProfileFound result, {String? eventIdPrefix}) {
  final p = result.profile;
  return UserProfile(
    pubkey: p.pubkey,
    name: p.name,
    displayName: p.displayName,
    about: p.about,
    picture: p.picture,
    banner: p.banner,
    website: p.website,        // ← stored in typed field
    nip05: p.nip05,            // ← stored in typed field
    lud16: p.lud16,            // ← stored in typed field
    rawData: const {},         // ← but rawData is empty
    createdAt: DateTime.now(),
    eventId: '${eventIdPrefix ?? 'rest'}-${p.pubkey}',
  );
}
```

`ProfileRepository.saveProfileEvent` (`mobile/packages/profile_repository/lib/src/profile_repository.dart:529`) then composes the Kind 0 content by spreading `currentProfile.rawData` first:

```dart
final profileContent = {
  if (currentProfile != null) ...currentProfile.rawData,    // empty for REST profiles
  'display_name': displayName,
  'about': about,
  'nip05': ?effectiveNip05,    // special-cased fallback to currentProfile.nip05 (lines 523-527)
  'picture': picture,
  'banner': banner,
};
```

Result: a profile loaded from the REST API loses everything that isn't explicitly in this dict on the next save. The nip05 special-case from #4022 is the only field that survives — `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, `bot`, `nip05_verified`, and any custom-client fields are dropped.

## Reproduction

1. User has a Kind 0 with `lud16`, `nip05`, `website`, `display_name`, `about`, `picture`, `banner` (e.g. published from another client like Damus, Amethyst, Primal).
2. User opens divine-mobile. The profile loads via the Funnelcake REST API path (`UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound`) — `rawData` is empty.
3. User taps Edit Profile, changes their bio or avatar, taps Save.
4. App publishes a Kind 0 containing only `{display_name, about, nip05, picture, banner}`. **`lud16` is gone.** **`website` is gone.** Any other custom field is gone.
5. Lightning zaps to this user's profile now fail; their website link disappears in other clients; etc.

This is a Nostr cross-client compatibility break — a divine.video user editing their bio in our app silently rewrites their public profile in a way that erases work done in any other client.

## Why the prior fix is not enough

#4022 added a targeted fallback inside `saveProfileEvent`:

```dart
final existingNip05 = (currentProfile?.rawData.containsKey('nip05') ?? false)
    ? null
    : currentProfile?.nip05;
final effectiveNip05 = resolvedNip05 ?? existingNip05;
```

That works for nip05 because `nip05` is one of the typed fields hoisted out of the raw event. But every *other* field that lives in Kind 0 needs the same treatment, and adding case-by-case fallbacks isn't sustainable — Kind 0 is an open dictionary by spec.

## Proposed fix

Pick one (in order of preference):

### Option A — REST returns the raw Kind 0 (best, requires funnelcake)

`/api/users/{pubkey}` and the bulk profile endpoints should include the raw Kind 0 event JSON (or at minimum the parsed `content` object) in the response. `UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound` then populates `rawData` from that. This restores the round-trip invariant that `currentProfile.rawData` contains every field the user has ever set.

Cross-repo coordination needed with divine-funnelcake — this is the right long-term fix.

### Option B — Fetch the live Kind 0 from a relay before publishing (mobile-only)

Before `saveProfileEvent` constructs the new content, query relays for the user's most recent Kind 0 and parse its content as the seed for `profileContent`, ignoring `currentProfile.rawData` entirely when it's empty. Slower (adds a round-trip on every Save) but doesn't require any funnelcake change and is robust against any REST-source mapping that drops fields.

### Option C — Mirror typed fields into rawData on REST construction (workaround)

In `UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound`, build `rawData` from the typed fields:

```dart
rawData: {
  if (p.name != null) 'name': p.name,
  if (p.displayName != null) 'display_name': p.displayName,
  if (p.about != null) 'about': p.about,
  if (p.picture != null) 'picture': p.picture,
  if (p.banner != null) 'banner': p.banner,
  if (p.website != null) 'website': p.website,
  if (p.nip05 != null) 'nip05': p.nip05,
  if (p.lud16 != null) 'lud16': p.lud16,
  if (p.lud06 != null) 'lud06': p.lud06,
},
```

Cheap, no network round-trip, fixes every field the typed layer already knows about — but **does not preserve fields the typed layer doesn't know about** (e.g. custom client fields, `bot`, future NIP additions). Should be an interim mitigation, not the final fix.

I'd recommend shipping Option C immediately as a stop-gap and tracking Option A or B as the durable solution.

## Impact

- Any divine-mobile user whose initial profile load goes through the REST API (which is the *primary* path now per the project's "always prefer funnelcake REST" guidance) and who edits their profile in our app.
- Loses lightning zaps until they re-add their lud16 in another client.
- Loses their website link, custom client fields, NIP-39 external identity proofs (if stored in Kind 0), etc.
- Cross-client experience: divine-mobile is a destructive editor for Kind 0 from the perspective of other Nostr clients.

## Related

- #4021 / #4022 — fix for nip05-specific symptom of this bug (merged 2026-05-06). The PR description and this issue's root-cause analysis are the same; #4022 just fixed one field.
- #2285 / #2294 — `UserProfile.fromFunnelcake()` factory introduced the empty `rawData: const {}`.

## Verification (for reviewer)

Reproduce by:
1. `git grep -n "rawData: const {}" mobile/packages/models/lib/src/user_profile.dart`
2. `git grep -n "...currentProfile.rawData" mobile/packages/profile_repository/`
3. Confirm via test: load profile via REST, edit display name only, assert published Kind 0 retains `lud16` from the prior event. (No such test exists today — the PR for the fix should add one.)

title: fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id>
body:
Closes #4178

## Summary

- Cold-start `divine.video/video/<sha256>` deep-links were stuck behind a generic spinner for 60s+ before rendering. Reorders `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` to local cache → Funnelcake REST → relay (each capped by a 3s timeout), so the canonical REST source answers first instead of running last after two relay round-trips that wait for EOSE from disconnected relays.
- Swaps the deep-link loading state from a generic Material `CircularProgressIndicator` to `BrandedLoadingIndicator` (matches the rest of the app).

## Why this was slow

`_VideoRouteCandidate.parse` treats a 64-char hex routeId as **both** an event id and a stable id. The previous flow ran:

1. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(ids:[hash], …)])` — never matches for Blossom-hashed share URLs (kind 34236 event ids are computed differently, the URL hash is the d-tag).
2. `_nostrClient.queryEvents([Filter(d:[hash], …)])` — may match.
3. Funnelcake REST.

`NostrClient.queryEvents` waits for EOSE from every relay in the pool with a 5s default timeout, and any relay still mid-connect during cold start blocks the whole batch. The on-relay-ready retry in `VideoDetailScreen` then re-runs the entire sequence on first relay connection. Worst case: ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake + relay-ready wait + ~5s + ~5s + Funnelcake = comfortably 60s.

REST is now first because it answers in <1s without waiting on relay state and is the canonical source for divine.video share URLs. Relay is kept as a fallback so events that only live on a user's personal relay still resolve.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/video_detail_screen_test.dart` — 11/11 pass (including updated `BrandedLoadingIndicator` assertions and the cold-start retry test)
- [x] `flutter test packages/videos_repository/` — 322/322 pass, including 4 new `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` tests:
  - resolves shared stable IDs via Funnelcake REST without hitting relay
  - falls back to relay when REST returns null (event only on personal relay)
  - falls back to relay when REST throws (e.g. `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`)
  - returns null without blocking when relay queries hang past the route timeout (verifies the in-source 3s cap fires)
- [ ] Manual: cold-launch app from `https://divine.video/video/c0614bf93911042dc9a3ea571b662ee7e69765e433ecc8468e5a727116577966`, verify branded indicator appears and player renders within ~1–2s.

title: context.watch causing unnecessary widget rebuilds

labels.name: performance
labels.description: App startup, video playback, rendering, and memory

body:
**Problem**

Some widgets use `context.watch<SomeBloc>()` to subscribe to an entire BLoC state but only read 1 field, causing rebuilds whenever any unrelated state field changes. `context.select` (or `BlocSelector`) should be used to subscribe to only the needed property.

**Evidence (examples)**

1. **`profile_videos_grid.dart` line 199**: `context.watch<BackgroundPublishBloc>()` watches the full state but only uses `.state.uploads` (filtered to active ones). `BackgroundPublishState` emits on every upload progress tick (progress field changes per upload). The grid rebuilds on every tick even though it only cares about which uploads exist and whether they have a result. This is the highest-impact occurrence because progress updates are frequent during upload.

2. **`video_editor_draw_item_indicator.dart` line 18**: `context.watch<VideoEditorDrawBloc>().state.selectedTool` watches full state but only reads `selectedTool`. `VideoEditorDrawState` has 7 fields. The indicator rebuilds when undo/redo availability, color, or stroke width change, none of which affect it.

3. **`profile_header_widget.dart` line 73**: `context.watch<MyProfileBloc>().state` watches a sealed class with 5 variants but only pattern-matches the `profile` field from `MyProfileUpdated`. Rebuilds on loading-to-loaded transitions, `isFresh` changes, `extractedUsername` changes, and error states, all irrelevant to the header's rendering.

**Done well**

`comment_item.dart` uses `BlocSelector<CommentsBloc, CommentsState, ({bool isUpvoted, bool isDownvoted, ...})>` to select exactly the 4 vote-related fields. `comments_screen.dart` uses `BlocSelector<CommentsBloc, CommentsState, CommentsSortMode>`. `my_followers_screen.dart` uses `BlocSelector<MyFollowingBloc, MyFollowingState, bool>`. These demonstrate the correct pattern.

**Impact**

Medium. #1 has the most room for improvement since upload progress emits many times per second during active uploads, triggering full grid rebuilds. #2 and #3 cause extra rebuilds on moderately interactive screens. None cause visible jank in isolation, but they add up and are worth addressing to keep new code on the right track.

**Effort**

Low. Each fix is a one-line change from `context.watch<Bloc>()` to `context.select<Bloc, T>((bloc) => bloc.state.field)`.

**Source**: [Code Review — Performance](docs/code-review/issues-performance.md)

title: feat: reduce npub prominence on edit profile, add external-account verifier (verifier.divine.video)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## What would you like?

Two related changes to the edit profile experience:

1. **De-emphasize the user's npub on the edit profile screen.** Today the read-only npub is rendered as a labeled top-level `TextFormField` ("Public key (npub)") in the form flow at `mobile/lib/screens/profile_setup_screen.dart:721-759`. The long string dominates the form and pushes more useful fields down. The npub still needs to be available (copy / share / key management) but does not need to be a primary edit-profile field. Some directions for the implementer / design (pick one, not all):
   - Collapse it behind a "Show technical details" disclosure.
   - Move it out of edit profile and into the existing key management screen (`mobile/lib/screens/key_management_screen.dart`).
   - Replace the inline display with a single "Copy public key" action (icon + label, no full string visible by default).

2. **Add an in-app entry point to an external-account verifier.** Where the npub used to live, surface a button/link that opens an in-app webview pointed at `verifier.divine.video` (planned external service). The verifier lets users prove ownership of accounts on other services (e.g. Twitter/X, GitHub, Mastodon, personal websites) tied to their Nostr pubkey. After verification, the verified accounts should be displayable as links on the user's bio/profile.

## How would this be useful for you?

- Edit profile becomes about the things people actually edit (display name, bio, avatar) instead of leading with a 60-character key string most users don't recognize.
- Lets users link out to their existing identities (Twitter, GitHub, Mastodon, personal site) with a verification trail, so followers can trust those links and find them on other platforms.
- Keeps Divine's identity story concrete and user-friendly: "Verify accounts" / "Add verified links to your profile" instead of cryptographic-key-as-UI.

## When would you use this?

- New user finishes onboarding, opens edit profile, and wants to add their existing Twitter/GitHub so people can find them — taps "Verify accounts", goes through the in-app verifier flow, comes back to a profile that shows verified links.
- Existing user wants to migrate their audience from another platform — adds a verified link to their old handle so followers recognize them.

## Scope (what this issue covers)

Mobile-side changes only:

- Reduce npub prominence on the edit profile screen (`profile_setup_screen.dart`).
- Add an entry point ("Verify accounts" / "Add verified links to your profile") that opens an in-app webview using the same pattern Divine already uses for external/integrated apps — **not** an external Safari/Chrome tab.
- Surface verified external accounts as tappable links on the user's bio/profile (read path).
- Follow Divine UI rules: VineTheme, dark-mode only, prefer full-screen flows over new dialogs/sheets.

## Out of scope

- Building / deploying `verifier.divine.video` itself. **This feature depends on that service existing** — flag as a prerequisite.
- Verifying *other people's* external accounts (this issue is only about the current user verifying their own).
- NIP-05 username verification (already exists; see closed #1539, #420).

## Open questions

- **Storage of verified accounts**: are these published as NIP-39 `i` tags on the user's kind 0 profile event (likely fit), as additional kind 0 fields, or fetched separately from a Divine-side service and rendered alongside the profile? Needs product / protocol confirmation before implementation.
- **Verifier handoff contract**: what does the verifier return to the app when the user completes a flow? URL fragment? postMessage? Needs to be defined together with the verifier service.
- **Removal/revocation**: how does a user un-verify or remove a previously verified link? Probably a subsequent profile edit — call out in design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the edit profile screen, the npub no longer occupies a top-level labeled field; it is reachable via copy action, disclosure, or the key management screen, but not visually dominant.
- [ ] The edit profile screen has an entry point that opens `verifier.divine.video` inside an in-app webview using the existing external-app pattern (not Safari/Chrome).
- [ ] After verification, verified external accounts appear as tappable links on the user's bio/profile.
- [ ] UI follows VineTheme, dark-mode only, full-screen flow preferred.
- [ ] Copy uses brand voice: candid, no jargon (e.g. "Verify accounts", "Add verified links to your profile" — not "Identity attestation").

title: task(providers): gate likes/comments/reposts repos on isNostrReady (Pattern A consistency)
body:
## Summary

Three Riverpod repository providers — `likesRepositoryProvider`, `commentsRepositoryProvider`, `repostsRepositoryProvider` — currently rebuild on `nostrServiceProvider` change but accept the placeholder `LocalKeySigner(null)` client without an `isNostrReady` gate. This is inconsistent with `profileRepositoryProvider` (`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart:1685`) and `pendingActionServiceProvider` (`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart:280-282`) which return `null` while `isNostrReady == false`, and is the root cause of the cold-launch race fixed downstream in #3503 / #3522.

The PR for #3503 patches the consequence at the BlocProvider boundary (composite `ValueKey` + `ref.watch` so the bloc swaps when the repo identity changes). This issue tracks the upstream consistency fix.

## Why this is its own issue

Extending Pattern A across the three repositories needs a UX decision that #3503's fix deliberately avoids: **what does the home-feed action button row render when the repository is `null`?** Today the BlocProvider unconditionally creates a `VideoInteractionsBloc`; with Pattern A the BlocProvider is gated on `repo != null`, and `LikeActionButton` / `RepostActionButton` / `CommentActionButton` would need a "not yet ready" state (disabled? hidden? placeholder skeleton?). That's designer-involved.

## Scope

Files to change (provider layer):

- `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`
  - `likesRepository(Ref ref)` → return type `LikesRepository?`; early-return `null` when `!ref.watch(isNostrReadyProvider)`
  - `commentsRepository(Ref ref)` → same shape
  - `repostsRepository(Ref ref)` → same shape

Files to change (consumer null-handling):

- `videoEventServiceProvider` (`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart:1430-1459`) — `setLikesRepository(likesRepository)` would need a null guard
- The four `BlocProvider<VideoInteractionsBloc>` sites in `mobile/lib/screens/feed/video_feed_page.dart` and `mobile/lib/screens/feed/pooled_fullscreen_video_feed_screen.dart` — gate the BlocProvider on `repo != null`
- `mobile/lib/screens/comments/comments_screen.dart`, `mobile/lib/screens/liked_videos_screen_router.dart`, `mobile/lib/widgets/profile/profile_grid.dart` — handle `null` repo

Tests:

- Unit-test the null gate in each provider
- Widget-test the BlocProvider sites for the unready state

## Out of scope

- The action-button "unready" UX is design's call. Recommend opening a small RFC with brand/design before implementation.

## Context

Investigation log + alternatives compared in PR #3522 description.

title: chore(backend): audit Funnelcake kind-34238 ingestion for self-acceptance events
body:
Follow-up to #3559 / #3566.

### Context

Before #3566 shipped, the inviter's own outgoing collaborator-invite card was rendered with Accept / Ignore on their conversation with the collaborator. Tapping Accept invoked \`CollaboratorResponseService.acceptInvite\` which signs and publishes a kind-34238 event with \`['p', creatorPubkey]\` set to the inviter's own pubkey — i.e. \`event.pubkey == creatorPubkey == p-tag value\`. Funnelcake ingests kind-34238 to drive collaborator-confirmation state.

Any tester who tapped Accept on their own outgoing card during the regression window may have produced one of these self-acceptance events on the relay / ingestion pipeline.

### Ask

1. Confirm whether Funnelcake's kind-34238 ingestion currently rejects events where \`event.pubkey == p-tag value\` (or \`event.pubkey == author of the addressable referenced by the \`a\` tag\`).
2. If not, add the filter and document the invariant on the ingestion side. The mobile client never publishes a legitimate self-acceptance.
3. Audit existing collaborator-confirmation rows for any that derive from a self-acceptance event ID. Clean up any rows that match.

### Why filed in mobile repo

Tracking with #3559 lineage so the QA / engineering thread is co-located. Implementation lives in the Funnelcake codebase — feel free to clone and re-file with backend tracking and link back here.

### Repro of the publish path

Pre-#3566:

1. As user A, post a video with user B as collaborator.
2. Open the DM with B.
3. Tap **Accept** on the (incorrectly rendered) outgoing card.

Wire-side: kind-34238 event with \`event.pubkey == A\`, \`['p', A]\`, \`['a', '<videoKind>:A:<dTag>']\`, \`['status', 'accepted']\`.

Post-#3566 the UI no longer surfaces Accept on sender-side cards and the cubit asserts in debug + early-returns in release if invoked, so this publish path is closed in the mobile client. The audit is purely about historical data on the ingestion side.

title: Transient duplicate video on own profile during collab accept via Connect
body:
When a collab is set up via connect.divine.video, the original Kind 34236 event is replaced with an updated version that includes the collaborator `p` tag. The author's mobile app briefly shows both the old and new versions on their profile before the replaceable event handler reconciles them.

## Observed behavior

Alice saw "Quiet spring dusk" twice on her own profile on mobile after setting up a collab via Connect. The duplicate resolved on its own after a short period. Not reproducible from another user's view of the same profile (verified from both web and a second mobile device).

## Root cause

Race between Funnelcake REST cache (serving the pre-collab version) and the relay subscription (delivering the updated version with collab tags). The `_handleReplaceableVideoEvent` dedup in `VideoEventService` and `_mergeVideoLists` in `ProfileFeedProvider` both handle this correctly in steady state, but there's a brief UI render window between the two data sources resolving.

## Relevant code

- `ProfileFeedProvider._canonicalVideoKey()` keys on `pubkey:stableId` (profile_feed_provider.dart:828)
- `VideoEventService._handleReplaceableVideoEvent()` deduplicates by `kind:pubkey:d-tag` (video_event_service.dart:2031)
- Both are correct for same-author replaceable events, but the race occurs when events arrive from different source paths (REST vs subscription) before the merge runs

## Suggested fix

Ensure that when `_mergeSourceVideos` or the subscription callback delivers a new version of a replaceable event, the UI state update is atomic with the old version removal. The current flow can render an intermediate state where both versions are present.

## Severity

Cosmetic, transient. Users won't understand why they see their own video twice, but it self-resolves. Only affects the author viewing their own profile at the moment a collab is accepted.

title: search: audit result surfaces for blocklist / visibility consistency
body:
## Summary

Search result surfaces need a consistent audit for blocklist, visibility, and filtering rules. We have prior fixes in this area, but they should be validated comprehensively instead of treated as one-off search bugs.

Parent epic: #3801

## Agent Brief

This issue is about **search result correctness across surfaces**.

Confirmed:
- We have at least one historical bug for blocked authors appearing in search results.
- A prior PR (#1204) fixed one path, but #948 remains open and should be reconciled.
- Search now spans people, videos, tags, and lists; correctness rules should be consistent.

Related issue:
- #948 — blocked author videos included in search results

## Problem

Search result filtering rules appear to have been fixed piecemeal. We need a unified audit so we know whether search respects blocklist and visibility rules across all result types and entry paths.

title: search: avoid misleading intermediate state during Explore → Search transition
body:
## Summary

The Explore → Search transition currently shows a brief intermediate full-screen state before meaningful search results are available. On slower connections this can feel like an error, flash, or hang rather than an intentional transition.

Parent epic: #3801

## Agent Brief

This issue is about the **intermediate visual state** during Explore → Search navigation.

Confirmed:
- Explore auto-pushes `/search-results/:query` on partial input.
- The search results screen becomes visible immediately.
- Real search work and useful results arrive later.
- Users can interpret the transient screen as broken or hung.

Do not collapse this issue into keyboard/focus behavior. They are related, but not identical.

## Confirmed facts

From reproduction logs:
- Explore route is active.
- App pushes `/search-results/:query` immediately after partial input.
- Search screen becomes visible in 2–3ms.
- Search results and timeout fallback occur meaningfully later.

From code:
- Explore pushes to `SearchResultsPage.pathForQuery(query)` from a debounced text listener.
- Search results view can render an idle/initial placeholder before async search state catches up.

## Problem

Users are seeing a route transition before the UI has a stable, intentional search state to present. The result is a visible intermediate screen that reads as a flash, error, or hang.

## Questions to resolve

- Should the route transition be delayed until search state is ready?
- Should Explore retain control until explicit submit?
- If the route transition stays, what exact loading/placeholder state should be shown?
- How should slow-network or timeout fallback be communicated?

## Acceptance criteria

- The Explore → Search transition no longer presents a misleading or broken-looking intermediate state.
- Slow-network behavior is intentional and visibly understandable.

title: epic(search): stabilize search UX, routing, focus, result quality, and technical debt
body:
## Summary

Search currently has multiple open issues across UX, routing behavior, keyboard/focus continuity, result quality, and implementation debt. These problems are related enough that we should track them under one parent issue and work from a shared problem statement.

This epic is **not a duplicate of #2470**.  `#2470` is the original feature umbrella for the unified Explore/Search experience. This issue is a **follow-on stabilization and technical debt epic** for the shipped behavior and the remaining gaps we now see in production and support feedback.

Status: active coordination epic

## Agent Brief

Use this issue as the parent context for all search stabilization work.

### Confirmed
- Explore search currently auto-navigates on partial input.
- Keyboard/focus continuity breaks during that transition.
- Search can show a misleading intermediate state before results load.
- People search can degrade under NIP-50 timeout fallback.
- Search behavior is entangled with existing routing/state/data-source debt.

### Do not assume
- that #2470 already covers stabilization work
- that the current UX is final or intended in its current form
- that all search bugs share the same root cause
- that a quick targeted fix is sufficient without checking architecture/test implications

### Expectations for child work
- Link child issues and PRs back to this epic.
- State clearly which confirmed problem is being addressed.
- Separate confirmed facts from inference.
- Avoid introducing more timer-driven UI coordination without explicit justification.
- Prefer testable state-driven behavior over UI-side implicit routing.

## Why this needs a parent issue

Today, the search problems are split across separate tickets with overlapping causes:

- UX/design intent vs. implemented behavior are not aligned.
- Routing and focus problems are coupled to the Explore → Search transition.
- Slow search/network fallback makes the transition feel worse and can be misread as an app hang.
- Some older search-result correctness bugs are still open or ambiguously resolved.
- The current implementation risks adding more debt unless we align fixes with the architecture/code-audit backlog.

A parent issue gives us one place to coordinate product, design, and engineering decisions.

## Relationship to existing search work

### Historical feature context
- #2470 — unified explore and search experience

### Why this is not a duplicate
- #2470 tracked the feature rollout and related implementation tasks.
- This epic tracks **stabilization, correctness, UX reconciliation, and technical debt reduction** after rollout.
- This issue should remain open until the current search experience is coherent, reliable, and aligned with both product intent and engineering standards.

## Current observed behavior

From recent reproduction logs and code review:

- Typing in Explore can auto-push the full-screen search route after a short debounce.
- The destination search screen does not consistently preserve keyboard continuity for continued typing.
- A transient intermediate search state appears before real results load.
- On slower connections, user search can hit NIP-50 timeout fallback, extending the “empty / flashing / hanging” perception.
- People search quality is not consistently reliable for finding the expected account.
- Search result correctness is still an active concern in some result surfaces.

## Confirmed facts

### Reproduced from logs
- Explore entered normally.
- App auto-navigated from Explore to `/search-results/:query` on partial input.
- This happened before any search result selection.
- Profile navigation happened only later, after search results were shown.
- `ProfileRepository.searchUsersProgressive` hit NIP-50 timeout fallback during search.

### Confirmed in code
- `mobile/lib/screens/explore_screen.dart`
  - `_onSearchChanged()` debounces input and pushes `SearchResultsPage.pathForQuery(query)` once query length is at least 2.
- `mobile/lib/screens/search_results/widgets/search_results_app_bar.dart`
  - the destination field only requests focus when `initialQuery` is empty
  - when navigated with a pre-filled query, it does not auto-focus

## Inferences

These are likely true, but should still be treated as interpretations rather than source-of-truth facts:

- The “keyboard stolen” report is caused by partial-input route navigation plus lack of destination focus transfer.
- The “weird flashing screen” perception is likely the transient intermediate search state becoming visible before meaningful results load.
- On slower networks, this intermediate state is likely interpreted by users as an error or hang.

## Open questions and decision owners

### 1. Search entry UX
Decision owner: Product / Design

Questions:
- Should Explore auto-navigate while typing?
- Should search results appear only on explicit submit/search action?
- If not, do we need an intermediate inline/typeahead state in Explore first?

### 2. Focus and keyboard continuity
Decision owner: Product / Design

Questions:
- If we do navigate during typing, should keyboard focus transfer seamlessly?
- Should the destination search field auto-focus when opened from partial input?

### 3. Intermediate / loading state
Decision owner: Product / Design

Questions:
- What should the user see between “started typing” and “search results available”?
- How do we avoid a placeholder flash that feels like an error or hang?
- What latency budget do we want for showing an intentional intermediate state?

### 4. People search reliability
Decision owner: Engineering

Questions:
- When NIP-50 search times out, what fallback chain should we use?
- Candidate fallback inputs:
  - local follow set
  - recent profile cache
  - indexer-backed profile search
  - some combination of the above
- What latency budget should govern when fallback results appear?
- What instrumentation is required so timeout/fallback behavior is diagnosable?

### 5. Search result correctness
Decision owner: Moderation / Policy + Engineering

Questions:
- Are all result surfaces consistently filtered for blocked users?
- Are people/videos/tags/lists following the same visibility and filtering rules?
- Which filtering rules are policy contracts vs implementation details?

## Existing related issues

### Directly related
- #3020 — keyboard collapses when navigating to search page when typing
- #3791 — cant find friends

### Search correctness / filtering
- #948 — blocked author videos included in search results

### Execution hierarchy
- GitHub child issues on this epic track active search execution work: #3791, #3802, #3803, #3804, #3805.
- #3020 remains a child of #2470 because it predates this stabilization epic and still has historical feature context there.
- #948 remains a child of #503 and should be reconciled against #1204 before any parent-hierarchy changes.

## Existing related PRs / implementation history

These are relevant descendants or related implementation work:
- #2950 — align Explore page theme with Figma design
- #2972 — return to originating tab when navigating back from search
- #2974 — fallback for unavailable list thumbnails
- #1204 — filter blocked authors from search results

## Technical debt dependencies

This epic is not only a product/UX cleanup. The issues below are the load-bearing architecture and reliability items most likely to shape search fixes and help us avoid creating more debt while we stabilize behavior.

### Architecture / State Management
- #3620 — Stop UI from bypassing BLoC layer  
  Search entry behavior is currently tightly coupled to UI text listeners and route pushes. We should move toward explicit state-driven behavior that is easier to test and reason about.

- #3621 — Complete state management migration (track ChangeNotifier)  
  Search spans multiple patterns today. Reducing mixed state management will make search UX, focus continuity, and result loading behavior more coherent.

- #3624 — Design unified caching architecture  
  Search quality depends on how cached, local, and remote data are combined. A clearer caching strategy is important for predictable search results and better slow-network behavior.

- #3627 — Document data source strategy for 4 read patterns  
  Search currently appears to mix relay, cache, and fallback/indexer behavior. This needs an explicit source-of-truth strategy.

### Routing / Navigation
- #3572 — Migrate GoRouter to @TypedGoRoute type-safe routing  
  Search is route-heavy and would benefit from stronger route contracts and less ambiguity around search-result/profile transitions.

### Error Handling / User State
- #3656 — Fix 4 screens with missing error state branches  
  Search should have explicit loading, empty, partial, and error states that do not feel like a flash, hang, or broken transition.

- #3592 — Add addError(e, stackTrace) to 54 BLoC catch blocks  
  Search and people discovery failures need better observability so timeouts and fallback states are diagnosable.

- #3593 — Document contracts for ~170 suppressed catch blocks  
  Search reliability work is harder while failure semantics remain unclear or suppressed.

- #3589 — Replace raw exception text in ~28 user-facing messages  
  Search/network failures should degrade gracefully with intentional user-facing language.

### Testing
- #3616 — Expand integration test coverage for major runtime flows  
  This search issue is a cross-screen runtime flow and should be covered by integration tests, not only isolated widget tests.

- #3608 — Write tests for 50+ untested services  
  Search repositories/services need stronger direct test coverage.

## Acceptance criteria for this epic

- We have a single approved product/design decision for Explore → Search behavior, documented in this issue or linked child issues.
- Keyboard/focus behavior for Explore → Search is explicitly defined and covered by widget or integration tests.
- Intermediate search-state behavior is explicitly designed, with a defined latency budget and instrumentation plan.
- People-search fallback behavior under NIP-50 timeout is documented as a concrete fallback chain, instrumented, and covered by tests where feasible.
- Search result filtering rules are documented and validated on all relevant result surfaces.
- Relevant architecture and test debt are linked so fixes reduce future churn instead of adding more debt.
- All child issues are linked and scoped under this epic.

## Out of scope

Unless explicitly pulled in later, this epic does not automatically include:
- generic non-search keyboard bugs
- unrelated feed/player regressions
- full search feature redesign beyond what is required to stabilize current behavior
- broad routing refactors unrelated to search paths

## Notes

- This epic is organizational and should not be closed by a single PR.
- Individual fixes should close child issues, not the epic itself.
- Some older search issues may need state cleanup or confirmation before being treated as active scope under this epic.
- Durable context should stay in this issue body rather than be scattered across comments.




---

`@NotThatKindOfDrLiz`

## Weekly Priority
`P1`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. decide and lock Explore -> Search interaction model
2. fix focus/keyboard continuity

5. clean up supporting debt only where needed

## Subgroup

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a product, design, or architecture decision is genuinely needed.

title: feat(dm): self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial sends
body:
## Description

Closes #4102 — the technical-debt follow-up to PR #3908.

When a NIP-17 send delivers to the recipient but the sender's
self-addressed gift wrap fails to publish, `ConversationBloc` emits
`SendStatus.sentPartial`. Tapping Retry on the SnackBar previously
redispatched the full `ConversationMessageSent` path, which republished
the recipient gift wrap and double-delivered the message. NIP-17 self
wraps are independent of recipient wraps — only the missing self wrap
needs to land on retry, never the recipient one. This PR adds the
self-wrap-only recovery primitive plus the matching BLoC event and
SnackBar wiring so Retry-on-`sentPartial` republishes only the sender's
gift wrap, leaving recipients untouched.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4102 (follow-up to #3908)

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Changes

**`NIP17MessageService` (`packages/dm_repository`)**
- New `publishSelfWrap({required Event rumorEvent})`: builds + publishes
  only the sender self-addressed gift wrap for a pre-existing rumor,
  sharing the underlying self-wrap helper with `sendRumor` so the two
  paths agree on null-builder, publish-failure, and exception handling.

**`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap(rumorId)`**
- Looks up the queue row by `rumorId`, rebuilds the rumor from
  `rumor_event_json` (preserving the receiver-side dedup key), publishes
  via `publishSelfWrap`, then deletes the row on success or marks
  `self_wrap_status: failed` for the next retry sweep.
- Idempotent against an already-sent row, defends against missing rows,
  foreign-owner rows (cross-account safety), corrupted rumor JSON, and a
  missing queue DAO.

**`DmRepository.sendGroupMessage`**
- Refactored to enqueue a queue row per recipient, mirroring
  `sendMessage`, and to write per-recipient outcomes inside the same
  transaction as the local message persist. This is what lets group
  recovery scope to only the affected successful recipient sends — the
  prior implementation shared a single send path with no queue rows, so
  partial group deliveries had nowhere to look up the rumor for replay.

**`ConversationState`**
- New `PartialSend({required List<String> rumorIds})` carries the
  per-recipient rumor ids whose self-wrap failed.
- `lastPartialSend` lives alongside `lastFailedSend` with its own clear
  flag in `copyWith`. The two states drive different recovery paths
  (full resend vs self-wrap-only), so they're tracked independently.

**`ConversationBloc`**
- On `sentPartial`, populates `lastPartialSend` (not `lastFailedSend`)
  with the rumor ids of the partial-self results.
- New `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested(rumorIds)` event with a
  `sequential()` transformer (same as `ConversationMessageSent`).
- The handler loops `recoverSelfWrap` per id, aggregates outcomes, and
  reduces `lastPartialSend.rumorIds` to only the still-failing ids so a
  second Retry tap targets exactly those.
- Removes the obsolete "TODO #3909" tradeoff comment block — the
  principled fix it described is now in place.

**`ConversationView`**
- `_onSendOutcome`'s SnackBar action branches on `sendStatus`:
  `sentPartial` dispatches `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested`,
  `failed` keeps dispatching `ConversationMessageSent`.

**l10n**
- No new keys. The existing `dmSendPartialMessage` and
  `dmSendFailedRetry` already exist in all 17 locales (added by PR
  #3908).

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `dart format` — no changes.
- [x] `mobile/packages/dm_repository` 217/217 passing (12 new tests:
  5 `publishSelfWrap`, 5 `sendGroupMessage` queue, 7 `recoverSelfWrap`).
- [x] `mobile/test/blocs/dm` + `mobile/test/screens/inbox` 311/311
  passing (4 new self-wrap recovery scenarios + 3 new event-equality
  tests + 3 new state-shape tests + 1 new view-test for retry-dispatch).

Pinning contracts added:
- `recoverSelfWrap` never publishes a recipient wrap (verified via
  `verifyNever(messageService.sendRumor(...))` and
  `verifyNever(messageService.sendPrivateMessage(...))` after recovery).
- `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` handler never calls
  `dmRepository.sendMessage` or `sendGroupMessage`.
- View test: tapping Retry on the partial-delivery SnackBar dispatches
  `ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` (not
  `ConversationMessageSent`).

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Force a self-wrap publish failure on a 1:1 send (e.g. block the
  second `publishEvent` round in a debug build) → SnackBar shows the
  partial-delivery copy → Retry resyncs the self-wrap without sending
  a second bubble to the recipient.
- [ ] Same for a group send where one of the per-recipient self-wraps
  fails → only that one rumor's self-wrap is republished on Retry.
- [ ] After a successful recovery, leave + re-enter the conversation —
  the `outgoing_dms` row for that rumor should be gone.

## Investigation notes

The plan in `tasks/lessons.md` shape, including the architectural
choice to enqueue group sends per-recipient (so partial group recovery
has a queue-row source of truth), was captured in /plan output for
#4102 prior to implementation.

title: DM: add self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial to avoid duplicate recipient delivery
body:
## Summary

`ConversationBloc` currently surfaces recipient-delivered / self-wrap-failed sends as `SendStatus.sentPartial` and offers a Retry action. That Retry re-dispatches the full `ConversationMessageSent` path, which republishes recipient wraps and can duplicate delivery to recipients who already received the message.

PR #3908 intentionally accepts that tradeoff because the current send stack has no primitive to retry only the sender self-wrap.

## Problem

The current recovery path is user-visible technical debt in the DM send flow:

- 1:1: retry after `sentPartial` can send the same DM to the recipient again.
- Group DM: retry can resend to the full recipient list even if only one successful per-recipient send had a self-wrap publication failure.

## Desired Outcome

Add a self-wrap-only recovery path so `sentPartial` can repair sender cross-device sync without re-delivering to recipients.

## Scope

- Introduce a repository/service API that can publish only the sender self-addressed NIP-17 gift wrap for an already-sent rumor.
- Preserve the `sentPartial` UX signal, but make Retry use the self-wrap-only path instead of the full send path.
- For groups, scope recovery to only the affected successful recipient sends.
- Add tests that pin no duplicate recipient publish on `sentPartial` recovery.

## Context

- Landed intentionally as a follow-up to PR #3908.
- Current tradeoff is documented in `conversation_bloc.dart`.
